**2026-10-06, a round on `kernel: Topology & data structure`'s own "Remove edge / collapse micro edge" bullet, count-neutral (stays 13/13/1, 27 items, 72.2%).** `Brep::RemoveSharedMicroEdge()` is generalized from requiring both endpoints to be isolated (touching nothing besides the micro edge and its own two designated per-face loop-neighbors) to tolerating any FURTHER edge at either endpoint too - closing the "a non-isolated (valence-4+...) shared micro-edge is still left alone" gap this bullet's own prior note named. A further edge belongs to some third (or later) face merely pinching at that same vertex, not to either of the two faces actually being merged across, so it is nudged to the shared merge point exactly like the two designated neighbors already are (the identical two-phase nudge-then-`ReplaceEdgeCurve()` primitive, just run for however many extra edges a vertex happens to carry) rather than refusing the whole call outright; `ReplaceEdgeCurve()`'s own re-trim handles whichever further face it borders for free, so no new topology-surgery code was needed, only a wider collection step ahead of the existing nudge/commit phases. Still refused: an edge touching both endpoints at once (would collapse to zero length), the identical "won't guess at a bowtie" discipline this method's own four-distinct-loop-neighbors check already applies elsewhere. Verified (`TestRemoveSharedMicroEdgeClosesSeamWithAThirdFacePinchingAtOneEndpoint`, tests/test_basic.cpp) on the existing isolated-case fixture plus a third face sharing only one point (a pure point-coincidence weld, no shared edge) with one of the two micro-edge endpoints, giving that vertex a real, directly-confirmed valence of 5 (not assumed) before the fix: the call now succeeds where it previously refused, both original faces collapse to triangles exactly as the isolated case already does, the third face's own loop and corner position are both confirmed undisturbed beyond the same micro-scale nudge the designated neighbors get, and the combined tessellated area is unchanged within tight tolerance. Does not flip this bullet's own `[partial]` status - still no general shared-edge collapse above tolerance, and no `dino8-app` command calls either `RemoveSharedMicroEdge` or `RemoveNakedMicroEdge` - so this category's own row and the kernel headline above are both unchanged. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite rebuilt and run clean end to end: 0 failures, 0 regressions; `ctest`'s own `dino8_kernel_smoke` re-run clean (1/1, 100%).

**2026-10-06, a round on `kernel: Local / direct-edit operations`: two real generalizations plus one honesty correction, no count change (stays 8/20/0, 64.3%).** (1) `Brep::SplitNakedEdgeAt` ("Split an edge at a point") is generalized from naked (1-trim) edges to a plain SHARED (2-trim) straight edge too — the ordinary two-manifold-edge case, resolving each of the edge's up to 2 trims against its own face's surface independently and splicing each one's own loop separately. A real, found-by-testing defect surfaced only once a genuinely shared edge was tried for the first time (a closed box, every edge shared): whichever of the two trims has `m_bRev3d == true` needs its new pair of trims spliced in with `bRev3d` flipped and in the matching relative order, not the naked-only unconditional `bRev3d == false` the original code always used — an earlier attempt that instead reversed the 2D curves themselves and kept `bRev3d == false` passed every structural check (same trim/edge counts) while silently producing a self-crossing loop on that one side, caught only by a 3x-too-large tessellated area. Verified on `Brep::FromPlanarFaces(CheckHealBoxFaces())`: splitting a shared edge now returns `Result::Ok`, both faces gain a trim each, and the box stays a genuinely valid, correctly-oriented, unit-volume solid (`TestBrepSplitNakedEdgeAtSplitsSharedEdgeOnBothFaces`, tests/test_basic.cpp) — still refuses a curved or non-manifold (3+ trim) edge exactly as before. (2) `Brep::ExtendFaceInPlace(face_index, direction, t0, t1, linear)` ("Extend a face/surface past its current boundary in place") is new: it extends one named face's own surface past one end of its current domain and rebuilds that face's trim loop/edges/corners to match, while every OTHER face of the same (possibly multi-face) Brep — including one genuinely SHARED with it on the far, non-extended side — is left completely untouched, closing the "detached into a brand-new separate object" half of this item's own disclosed gap for the common case of extending AWAY from a neighbour. Scoped to an untrimmed (natural-domain-rectangle), single-end extension whose extended cap and both rail trims are naked; extending TOWARD a shared edge is refused. Hit and fixed a real `ON_SurfaceProxy` caching bug along the way (`ON_BrepFace::SetProxySurface()` must be called again after changing `m_si`, mirroring what `ON_Brep::NewFace(int)` itself already does — confirmed directly in OpenNURBS' own source, not assumed; without it `SurfaceOf()`/`Domain()` kept reporting the OLD domain and crashed deep inside `EvPoint` during `SetTolerancesBoxesAndFlags()`). Verified on a hand-built two-face planar bracket genuinely sharing one edge: the extended face's own area matches the exact closed-form extended-rectangle value, and the untouched neighbour's own surface index, shared edge (2-trim count, exact 3D endpoints), and area are all bit-for-bit unchanged (`TestBrepExtendFaceInPlaceNakedSideGrowsExactRectangleAndLeavesSharedNeighbourUntouched`/`TestBrepExtendFaceInPlaceRefusesTowardSharedEdgeAndOutOfScopeInputs`, tests/test_basic.cpp). (3) Honesty correction on "Edge blend removal": its own "throws for oblique-end cylindrical fillets" clause was stale — `RemoveBlend` already inverts an oblique-end cylindrical fillet via the same `CollapseNotchRun` splice the conical case uses, per `fillet.h`'s own current doc comment and the already-registered `TestRemoveBlendRoundTripsAnObliqueEndFillet`/`TestRemoveBlendRoundTripsAnObliqueEndConcaveFillet` (re-confirmed passing this pass); the remaining "shares a cylinder with a second spherical corner" restriction is kept, accurate. None of the three crosses `[partial]` → `[present]` (both (1) and (2) remain deliberately narrow — straight/shared edges only, curved still refused; untrimmed single-end-only extensions away from a neighbour only — and (3) is a text-only correction), so this category's own count stays 8 present / 20 partial / 0 missing (28 items, 64.3%). Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite rebuilt and run clean: 9416 checks, 0 failures, 0 regressions (up from 9238 before this session's own merge + additions).

**2026-10-05, first dedicated rotation on `kernel: Tessellation / faceting` (tessellation) - this category had never had a dedicated session before, despite being tied for rank 4 of 17 kernel categories by weight/remaining-items: both of its own `[missing]` bullets close `[missing]` -> `[present]`, moving the row 14/9/2/25 (74.0%) -> 16/9/0/25 (82.0%).** (1) **Angular tolerance control exposed as a general faceting-quality knob**: every existing adaptive tessellator in this kernel (`SuggestedDivisions`/`SuggestedParameterValues`, `TessellateGridAdaptive` and siblings, `Brep::TessellateAdaptive`/`TessellateNonUniformAdaptive`) only ever took a LINEAR `chord_tolerance`, back-solving a turning-angle bound from it via the sagitta formula - an angle itself was never a knob a caller could set directly. A full `ByAngle` sibling family now exists at every level: `NurbsCurve::SuggestedSamplesByAngle`/`SuggestedParameterValuesByAngle` (curve.h/curve.cpp), `NurbsSurface::SuggestedDivisionsByAngle`/`SuggestedParameterValuesByAngle`/`TessellateGridAdaptiveByAngle`/`TessellateGridNonUniformAdaptiveByAngle`/`TessellateGridClippedExactAdaptiveByAngle` (surface.h/surface.cpp), and `Brep::TessellateAdaptiveByAngle`/`TessellateToClosedMeshAdaptiveByAngle` (brep.h/brep.cpp) - a whole-body tessellation call can now take a maximum facet-turning-angle bound directly, validated to `(0, pi]`, with no chord-height conversion anywhere in the path. (2) **Post-tessellation deviation verification**: no function anywhere measured whether a resulting mesh actually stayed within the tolerance it was tessellated for. `NurbsSurface::MeasureGridTessellationDeviation(u_divisions, v_divisions, samples_per_triangle)` (surface.h/surface.cpp) closes this - it reconstructs `TessellateGrid`'s own exact grid and diagonal convention, samples several INTERIOR barycentric points per triangle (deliberately not the corners, which trivially coincide with the true surface by construction), and measures each sample's true-surface point against the flat facet's own interpolated point at the same location, returning the worst deviation found. See each bullet's own note above (category section below, "kernel: Tessellation / faceting") for full construction, and a genuine, honestly-disclosed cross-check finding from building (2): probing `SuggestedDivisions(chord_tolerance)`'s own resulting resolution with the new measurement function shows the real, full 2D facet deviation consistently runs ~1.03-1.09x ABOVE `chord_tolerance` itself - not a bug in either function, but a previously-unmeasured gap between the existing single-direction sagitta estimate and the true facet deviation this new function is the first to actually measure. A second genuine finding surfaced verifying (1) against a full circle: this kernel's real `ON_Circle::GetNurbForm()` representation (a 4-span rational quadratic with double knots at each 90-degree boundary) has demonstrably non-uniform PARAMETER SPEED within each span, confirmed to affect the pre-existing chord-based `SuggestedParameterValues()` identically at a tight enough tolerance - constant geometric curvature does not imply constant parameter speed for a rational conic, a wrong assumption this session caught in its own first draft test (which asserted uniform breakpoint spacing) before trusting it, and corrected to assert the real guarantee instead (every final segment's own tangent turning genuinely stays within `angle_tolerance`). This category's own weight/remaining-items ratio (the "Priority order for maximum score-per-fix" ranking) moves from 1/11 = 0.091 (tied for rank 4) to 1/9 = 0.111 - see that table's own dated note below for the final combined ranking (a tie with Curve operations, not a standalone rank 3). This session's own isolated headline derivation (70.8% -> 71.3%) is superseded by the merge-reconciliation note above, which combines this row's change with a concurrent Curve operations session's own row change to get the correct combined **71.5%**. **2026-10-05, a round on `kernel: Topology & data structure`: `TrimmedPlanarFaceWelded()` closes the straight-edged half of the "Genuine topology produced by every constructor" bullet's own named gap for `TrimmedPlanarFace()`, no count change (stays 13/13/1, 27 items, 72.2%).** `Brep::TrimmedPlanarFaceWelded(surface, trim_loop_uv, hole_loops_uv)` (brep.h; brep.cpp) is the "Welded" sibling `BoxWelded()` already established for `Box()`, applied to the one remaining surface-only factory whose own boundary is already a plain straight-edged polygon rather than an analytic curve: it maps `trim_loop_uv`/each hole to 3D via `surface.PointAt(u, v)`, fits a plane via this file's own existing `NewellNormal()` helper, and composes the existing, already-tested `FromPlanarFaces()` (outer loop) with `AddHoleLoop()` (one call per hole) — real shared vertices/edges and a genuine `ON_BrepLoop::outer`/`::inner` pair, `raw().IsValid()` true, unlike `TrimmedPlanarFace()`'s own bare `NewFace(int)` side-table polygon. A genuine, incidental finding while building this evidence: `TrimmedPlanarFace()`'s own pre-existing test asserts a tessellated area of 36.0 for a trim loop whose true analytic area is 49.0 - its default `exact_clip=false` whole-cell tessellation quantizes to its own 6x6-unit-cell approximation rather than the exact figure, confirmed directly via a `dino8_scratch_test` probe rather than assumed; `TrimmedPlanarFaceWelded()`'s own real trim boundary tessellates to the correct exact 49.0 instead. A holed face's own `Tessellate()` call was found NOT to reproduce an exact analytic area either, even though the face itself is entirely flat (the same honesty the `MergeSameSurfaceFaces` bullet already discloses for an analogous curved-face case) - verified via `LoopCount()`/`TypeOfLoop()` classification and a bounded (not exact) area check instead. **2026-10-05, round 7 on `kernel: Offsetting, shelling, thickening` (offsetshell), count-neutral:** the prior round on this category closed Round-style corners for `NurbsCurve::OffsetInPlane()`'s own exact polyline case; this round picks up the two closest remaining gaps that same pass's own "Still partial" text named - Chamfer/Smooth/None corner modes, and the category's long-standing "Offset self-intersection / invalid-loop removal" item. (1) **`CurveOffsetCornerStyle::Chamfer`** (curve.h/curve.cpp) closes the Chamfer half of the "Curve offset corner handling at kinks" bullet's own disclosed gap: a FILL corner (the same convex, gap-opening side `Round` already special-cases) is now cut with the single straight segment directly between the two simple per-edge offset tangent points `T0`/`T1` - literally `Round`'s own arc chord, needing no angle or sweep-direction solve at all - while a CROSS (concave/contracting) corner is left at the exact Sharp miter point either way, identical to `Round`. `BuildRoundOffsetCorner()`'s own `has_arc`/`arc` fields are generalized to `has_piece`/`piece` to host either style's own corner geometry without duplicating the surrounding per-edge assembly loop. Verified (`tests/test_basic.cpp`) on the same fixtures `Round`'s own tests already establish: on the open 4-vertex polyline's two 90-degree fill corners, the result passes through both tangent points AND the chord's own independently-computed midpoint (at radius `1/sqrt(2)` from the vertex) while passing through neither Sharp's own (farther) corner nor Round's own (farther still) bisector point (`TestCurveOffsetInPlaneChamferStyleCutsConvexCorners`); on the L-tromino reflex fixture, the one concave corner stays at exactly Sharp's own miter point while its convex neighbors are genuinely cut (`TestCurveOffsetInPlaneChamferStyleLeavesConcaveCornerAsExactMiter`); and a closed square's own Chamfer offset closes its wraparound seam exactly, with total `Length()` matching the independent closed-form perimeter of a chamfered square (4 full-length sides plus four straight 45-degree chords of length `distance*sqrt(2)`) - strictly shorter than the Round-style perimeter at the same distance, since a chord is always shorter than its own arc (`TestCurveOffsetInPlaneChamferStyleClosedSquareMatchesClosedFormPerimeter`). (2) A new `IsOffsetPolygonSimple()` helper (curve.cpp) closes the "not even detected" half of the "Offset self-intersection / invalid-loop removal" bullet's own disclosed gap for this one exact case: a CLOSED polyline's exact Sharp miter polygon is now checked via `detail::IsSimplePolygon()` (the same proper-edge-crossing test boolean.cpp/surface.cpp's own concave-trim code already relies on, applied here to the offset result rather than a trim loop) and refused (`Result::Failed`) if two non-adjacent edges properly cross, instead of silently returning the bowtied loop as `Result::Ok` - detection only, not repair, the same honest "detect, don't repair" convention this file's other feasibility guards already follow. The right fixture mattered here: an initial "comb with one slot" fixture turned out to degenerate into a COLLINEAR edge overlap rather than a proper transversal crossing at the distance that closes its slot (`SegmentsProperlyIntersect()`'s own documented caveat excludes collinear overlap by design, so that fixture never actually exercised the new guard) - caught by directly probing the built library across several candidate fixtures/distances before trusting any of them, not assumed from the construction alone. The L-tromino reflex fixture already established above, shrunk inward (a negative distance) far enough to invert its own two arms past each other, does produce a genuine detected crossing; verified both that a safe inward distance well within either arm's own thickness still succeeds cleanly, and that a distance which collapses the shape past itself is now refused (`TestCurveOffsetInPlaneClosedPolygonRefusesSelfIntersectingLoop`). Neither change adds a new row or flips an existing one: "Curve offset corner handling at kinks" and "Offset self-intersection / invalid-loop removal" were already `[partial]` and stay `[partial]` - Smooth/None corner modes still don't exist, no app command calls `OffsetInPlane` with anything but the implicit Sharp default, and curve/surface/body self-intersection REPAIR (as opposed to this pass's own detection) is still entirely unrepaired, the same disclosed limit named before this pass. `kernel: Offsetting, shelling, thickening`'s own row (3/24/0 of 27, 55.6%) and every headline number at the top of this document are unchanged. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite (direct binary run, from-scratch build in this environment): 8910 checks passing, 0 regressions, confirmed via the binary's own terminal "all checks passed"/exit-0 signal and a count of the full captured run's own `ok:` lines; `ctest --test-dir dino8-kernel/build` also re-run clean (100% tests passed, 1/1).*

**2026-10-01, a round on `kernel: Local / direct-edit operations`: two genuine batch-sibling additions and one topology generalization, no count change (stays 8/20/0, 64.3%).** (1) `SplitFaceByCurves(target, face_index, curves, tolerance, samples)` (boolean_general.h/.cpp) is the batch sibling of `SplitFaceByCurve()` (that bullet's own item, "Split face by curve / surface"): `curves` is a caller-chosen list of independent open curves, all handed to `FragmentFaces()` as separate chains on the same face in ONE call, so N non-crossing curves split a face into N+1 fragments in a single pass rather than through N-1 sequential two-way splits. Verified on the box's own flat top face (area 16) cut by two independent parallel lines (x=-0.5/x=0.5): one call produces exactly 3 strips with the exact closed-form areas (6, 4, 6) the two cuts imply (`TestSplitFaceByCurvesBoxTopFaceTwoParallelCutsProduceThreeStrips`, tests/test_basic.cpp); two curves that cross each other mid-face are refused (the actual fragment count no longer matches `curves.size() + 1`, caught rather than silently returned, `TestSplitFaceByCurvesRejectsCrossingCurves`). (2) `ImprintClosedCurvesOnFace(target, face_index, curves, tolerance, samples)` is the identical batch generalization of `ImprintClosedCurveOnFace()` ("Imprint curve / face onto a body face"), for independent closed interior loops instead of open chains: `FragmentFaces()`'s own closed-chain pass already finds each loop's own owning fragment independently, so N disjoint loops become N holes bridged into one outer fragment plus N separate interior disks in one call. Verified with two disjoint 1x1 holes on the same top face, producing exactly the 1/1/14 area split in one call (`TestImprintClosedCurvesOnFaceBoxTopFaceTwoHoles`). (3) `Brep::MergeCoplanarFaces()` ("Merge coplanar adjacent faces") is generalized from "exactly one shared edge" to "one maximal CONTIGUOUS run of manifold-safe shared edges" — a shared boundary later subdivided into several collinear trims (e.g. by an imprint, or a T-junction split applied to only one side) is now merged in one pass; two genuinely SEPARATE shared edges are still refused (`TryMergeCoplanarPair()`'s own `build_path()`, brep.cpp, now walks and validates the whole run instead of one fixed index). Verified on two coplanar unit squares whose shared edge is pre-split into 2 collinear trims on each side (an extra vertex at the midpoint): one `MergeCoplanarFaces()` call still welds them into a single face of the exact 2.0 combined area (`TestMergeCoplanarFacesWeldsAdjacentSquaresSharingTwoCollinearTrims`). None of the three crosses any item from `[partial]` to `[present]` — all three remain scoped exactly as their own bullets below already disclose (no app wiring for any of the three kernel APIs; `SplitFaceByCurves`/`ImprintClosedCurvesOnFace` inherit every single-curve scope limit their own non-batch sibling already has) — so this category's own count stays 8 present / 20 partial / 0 missing (28 items, 64.3%). Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite rebuilt and run clean: 8519 checks, 0 failures, 0 regressions (up from 8470).

**2026-10-04, a round on `kernel: Local / direct-edit operations`: one shared-helper generalization across two already-`[partial]` items, no count change (stays 8/20/0, 64.3%).** `MoveConvexPlanarPoints()`'s shared core (`dino8-kernel/src/boolean.cpp`), used by `MoveVertexConvexPlanar`/`MoveVerticesConvexPlanar`/`MoveEdgeConvexPlanar`/`MoveEdgesConvexPlanar` (the "Move a single B-rep vertex directly"/"Move/transform edge" bullets below), used to refuse outright any face incident to a moved point with more than 3 corners, on the reasoning that only a triangle's plane is always well-defined regardless of where one corner sits. This pass replaces that vertex-count proxy with a direct planarity check: a touched face's new plane is now derived via Newell's method (`PolygonNewellNormalRaw()`, boolean.cpp — the same summed-cross-product-over-every-edge formula `brep.cpp`'s own `NewellNormal()` and `mesh.cpp`'s own `NewellNormal()` already use elsewhere in this codebase to find a polygon's own normal directly from its vertices, this TU keeping its own small copy per that existing precedent rather than sharing one across a header) instead of a plain two-edge cross product — mathematically identical for a TRIANGLE, since every other edge's own contribution to the sum vanishes identically, so every pre-existing triangle-only test (e.g. the pyramid-apex and tetrahedron fixtures already in this family) is completely unaffected — and, for a 4+-sided face, every one of its own corners (the moved one(s) included) is now checked directly against the resulting plane rather than refused by corner count alone. A 4+-sided face's own UNMOVED corners already pin its plane exactly (any 3 non-collinear points do), so a moved corner is only ever accepted when it genuinely lands back within that same plane — e.g. one or two corners of a quad sliding sideways within that quad's own existing plane — and a move that would leave the face genuinely non-planar still throws `std::invalid_argument`, exactly as before, just via this direct check instead of a vertex-count gate. Verified on `MakeTestPyramid()`'s own quad base (unlike its apex, already exercised by this bullet's own pre-existing test): sliding one base corner, and separately a whole base edge (both of its corners), within the base's own z=0 plane reshapes it into an irregular (non-rectangular) quadrilateral whose exact shoelace area — computed independently via a new `QuadAreaShoelaceXY()` test helper — gives, through the classical pyramid volume formula `(1/3)*base_area*height` (valid for ANY planar polygon base, not just a rectangle), hand-derived expected volumes of 500 and 600 respectively (up from the original 400), matched to the measured result rather than merely plausible-looking numbers (`TestMoveVertexConvexPlanarQuadBaseCornerWithinPlaneMatchesExactVolume`/`TestMoveEdgeConvexPlanarQuadBaseEdgeWithinPlaneMatchesExactVolume`, tests/test_basic.cpp); the identical corner move taken OFF that plane (nonzero z) is still correctly refused, now via the new planarity check rather than the old, removed "not a triangle" gate, but the identical `std::invalid_argument` failure mode callers already handle (`TestMoveVertexConvexPlanarRefusesNonPlanarQuadCornerMove`). A box's own corner or edge — each incident face's plane ALSO pinned by a THIRD, independent quad through every touched vertex — is still correctly refused by every pre-existing test, unchanged: no position but the original one can lie in all three of those planes through a shared corner at once, a genuine mathematical limit on this family, not merely an unimplemented case. See each bullet's own same-day follow-up note below for the full per-function detail. Neither item crosses `[partial]` → `[present]`: convex-planar-faced solids only and no `dino8-app` command wiring remain for both, exactly as each bullet's own paragraph already discloses — only the "every incident face must be a triangle" restriction narrows to "every incident face must stay genuinely planar," a strictly larger, directly-checked scope rather than a vertex-count proxy for it. This category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts (8/20/0, 28 items, 64.3%) and the kernel headline (70.5%) above are therefore unchanged by this pass. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite rebuilt from scratch and re-run clean on the fully-merged branch: 8782 checks, 0 failures, 0 regressions (up from 8769, 13 new).

**2026-10-05, a round on `kernel: Local / direct-edit operations`: one real narrowing, no count change (stays 8/20/0, 64.3%).** `PushPullFace()`'s/`PushPullFaces()`'s own "a pull refuses an oblique (non-perpendicular) neighbour" restriction is lifted: the half-space clip a pull's own retrim already ran (`SplitByHalfspace()`, `detail/halfspace_clip3d.h`) was always a genuine, exact 3D-plane clip regardless of a neighbour's own orientation - the actual bug was in `new_loop` itself, which used to translate every one of the pulled face's own boundary vertices uniformly along its normal, silently WRONG the moment an incident neighbour's own plane doesn't contain that normal direction (an oblique neighbour), leaving a gap between the new cap and that neighbour's own correctly-clipped boundary. New private helper `PushPullCorrectedVertex()` (`dino8-kernel/src/boolean.cpp`) fixes this directly: at a Brep vertex where the pulled face meets two neighbours, a THIRD edge - shared between those two neighbours themselves - runs into the solid's own interior, and clipping either neighbour against the same cut plane finds its own crossing point on that identical physical edge, so both independently agree on the corrected vertex position regardless of either neighbour's own orientation; `new_loop`'s own corner is now this real intersection (found via new helper `FindSharedEdgeIndices()`, extending `FacesShareEdge()`'s own match to also report where it is in each loop) instead of a blind per-vertex offset - reducing algebraically to the exact same point the old offset already gave for a perpendicular neighbour, so every pre-existing test in this family is unaffected. Verified on a genuine frustum (`DraftFacesConvexPlanar` tilting all 4 walls of a 10x10x10 box, confirmed not perpendicular to the top cap's own normal): pulling the top face down by 4 matches the classical frustum-of-a-pyramid volume formula at the new height exactly (530.88 to 1e-9 relative, not the wrong volume a blind translate would give), and the new top cap lands on the exact concentric `[0.6,9.4]` square the frustum's own linear taper implies, not the old `[1,9]` square merely shifted down (`TestPushPullFaceObliqueNeighbourMatchesExactFrustumVolume`, tests/test_basic.cpp); `PushPullFaces()`'s identical fix is verified to match `PushPullFace()`'s own output bit-for-bit on the same fixture (`TestPushPullFacesObliqueNeighbourMatchesPushPullFace`). See the "Push/pull a face" bullet below for the full construction and test detail. Doesn't flip this item's own rating or this category's own counts (already `[partial]`, stays `[partial]`: planar-faced-only and no app wiring remain). Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite rebuilt and run clean: 9238 checks, 0 failures, 0 regressions (up from 9170).

**2026-10-01, a session on `kernel: Feature operations`: three batch-hole additions, no category score change.** `dino8::kernel::MakeHoles()`/`MakeCounterboreHoles()`/`MakeCountersinkHoles()` (dino8-kernel/include/dino8/kernel/boolean_general.h; src/boolean_general.cpp) are plural siblings of `MakeHole()`/`MakeCounterboreHole()`/`MakeCountersinkHole()`, each closing those functions' own disclosed "one hole per call" limitation for the common case of several identically-sized holes sharing one axis direction (a bolt circle or a grid of mounting holes). **2026-10-01, a session on `kernel: Feature operations`: three closures, one a genuine `[missing]` → `[partial]` flip.** (1) **Lattice/cellular infill** (`[missing]` → `[partial]`): `dino8::kernel::LatticeInfill()` (dino8-kernel/include/dino8/kernel/features.h; src/features.cpp) is this kernel's first cellular-infill code of any kind — a strut-based cubic lattice, not a gyroid/TPMS or Voronoi infill (both remain genuinely unimplemented) — built from `Mesh::Cylinder()` struts unioned together (one real Boolean Union per strut, needed because several struts converging on a shared grid node genuinely overlap in volume there, not merely touch — a confirmed, fixed pitfall: two COLLINEAR struts meeting flush end-to-end at a shared node are a genuinely hard degenerate tangency, giving a `IsClosedManifold()` but measurably too-small volume until every strut is extended by `strut_radius` at both ends) and trimmed to the target solid via a real `BooleanCombine()` Intersection. (2) **Sheet-metal features** (no count change, already `[partial]`): `dino8::kernel::MultiBend()` (sheet_metal.h/.cpp) generalizes `Bend()` from a single bend to an N-bend chain (a U-channel/hat-channel, each bend free to use its own radius), closing the item's own disclosed "no multi-bend flat pattern" gap — reduces EXACTLY to `Bend()`'s own construction at N=1; a confirmed finding along the way (`dino8_scratch_test` angle/leg-length sweeps) is that `Brep::Extrude()`'s own star-shaped capping limit shrinks much faster across a CHAIN of bends than across `Bend()`'s own single one, so a real chain stays valid only at short legs and modest (roughly 10-20 degree) per-bend angles, not the dramatic 90-degree turns a single `Bend()` call tolerates. (3) **Emboss/deboss** (no count change, already `[partial]`): `dino8::kernel::EmbossProfileWithHoles()` (boolean_general.h/.cpp) extends `EmbossProfile()` to a profile with one or more holes, closing the item's own disclosed "lettering with disconnected glyph counters (an 'O' or 'A''s own hole)" gap — each hole's own tool is placed by which boolean op it will combine with (not simply copying the outer tool's own margin convention, which was tried first and found to silently build an invalid result), refilling/re-cutting that hole's footprint flush with the surface. Two further pre-existing `BooleanCombineGeneral()` limitations surfaced while testing this, neither worked around: a large-enough absolute outer radius makes this two-boolean-op composition measurably more tolerance-sensitive than either op alone (an invalid `ON_Brep` at radius 3.0 on this bullet's own fixture, valid at radius 1.0 - what both new tests actually use); and two axis-aligned, edge-parallel polygon profiles (a square hole in a square outer profile) can separately hit a coincident-face degeneracy, confirmed the same way against a hand-written two-step composition with no helper function involved - a round profile at modest scale is unaffected. See each bullet's own note below for full construction and test detail (8 new tests total, tests/test_basic.cpp). Only the Lattice/cellular infill closure changes this category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts — Feature operations moves 6/17/1 (24 items, 60.4%) → 6/18/0 (24 items, 62.5%). The app headline is unaffected by this pass (no `dino8-app` command wires any of these three in yet). Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite re-run clean, 0 regressions, after adding these (8298 checks).

**2026-10-01, a fifth kernel rotation on "Intersections & projections" (the single highest-ranked kernel category by weight/remaining-items per this document's own "Priority order for maximum score-per-fix" section - see below): two bullets close `[partial]` → `[present]`, neither by reusing an existing general-purpose function naively (the same "not usable for this without a dedicated fix" trap this category's own `IntersectCurves(c, c)`/`IntersectSurfaces(s, s)` caveats already name elsewhere).**

(1) **Surface / B-rep self-intersection detection**: this bullet's own last remaining half - "no face-interior self-intersection test" (a single face folding back onto itself, as opposed to `FindBrepSelfIntersections()`'s own face-VS-face test, already `[present]`) - is closed by the new `FindFaceInteriorSelfIntersections(brep, opt)` (dino8-kernel/include/dino8/kernel/surface_intersect.h; src/surface_intersect.cpp). A naive `IntersectSurfaces(s, s, opt)` is NOT usable here for the identical reason `IntersectCurves(c, c)` already isn't for curve self-intersection: every point trivially coincides with itself under its own parametrization, so a naive self-SSX reports nearly the whole surface as "self-intersecting." The fix mirrors `IntersectCurveSelfIntersections()`'s own established answer one dimension up: seed ONLY triangle pairs from the surface's own regular tessellation grid (`SurfaceMesh::nu`/`nv`, now tracked - a small, additive struct change) whose grid CELLS are separated by at least 2 cells (Chebyshev distance) - the 2D analogue of "at least 2 segments apart" - skipping a smoothly-varying patch's own ordinary local neighbourhood (always close in 3D too, not a crossing) while still catching a genuine fold-back between topologically distant regions. Each surviving candidate pair's `TriTri` crossing segment (the exact triangle/triangle test `IntersectSurfaces()` itself already uses) seeds a Newton refinement of the true `Sa == Sb` system (`RefineSurfaceSurfacePoint()`, called with the SAME surface as both arguments - purely mechanical, since that function only ever calls `.PointAt()` on each argument independently); a result that converges back onto the trivial `ua==ub`/`va==vb` diagonal is discarded as that trap, not a real second preimage. Reported as isolated POINTS (`FaceInteriorSelfIntersection{face_index, point, uv_a, uv_b, gap}`), not stitched into curves - the same honestly-scoped choice `FindSurfaceTangentContacts()` already makes for an analogous reason (a single surface's own trivial-diagonal trap complicates chaining enough that point-level detection is the honest stopping point this round). Verified by `TestFindFaceInteriorSelfIntersectionsDetectsFoldedFace` (tests/test_basic.cpp): a single B-rep face built by extruding a degree-1 "bowtie" profile (the same self-crossing corners `TestIntersectCurveSelfIntersectionsFindsBowtieAndRejectsSimpleCurves`'s own fixture uses, (0,0)->(10,10)->(10,0)->(0,10) in x/z) straight along Y reports at least one hit, every hit landing at the profile's own hand-derivable (x=5, z=5) crossing with two genuinely distinct (u, v) preimages (not the trivial diagonal); a plain flat (non-self-crossing) extruded face reports zero. Still honestly scoped: point detections only, no continuous self-intersection curve; the trim filter is a per-triangle centroid test (sampling-resolution-limited, the same honesty this file's other trim-aware functions already carry); and no `dino8-app` command calls it yet.

(2) **Pullback of a 3D curve to surface parameter space**: this bullet's own text had gone stale - a general-purpose public pullback call (`PullbackCurveToSurface`'s `pcurve` field) already existed, added when the separate "Pull curves/points to surfaces" bullet closed, but that closure's own note explicitly flagged why THIS bullet stayed `[partial]` regardless: "`pcurve`... does not close the separate... bullet below - that one stays `[partial]` on its own honestly-disclosed periodic-seam limitation" (see that note above). This rotation closes exactly that limitation: `pcurve`'s own fit now unwraps the raw per-sample (u, v) sequence across any CLOSED surface direction before fitting (`PullbackCurveToSurface`, src/surface_intersect.cpp) - whenever two consecutive samples in a closed direction differ by more than half that direction's domain length, the later one is shifted by a whole period first, so the cubic keeps moving the way it was already moving instead of swinging through the domain's middle (the same seam-unwrap idea `LerpUV`/`SplitAtSeams` already apply elsewhere in this file, applied here to a GLOBAL fit instead of one linear step). `pcurve`'s own control points can therefore legitimately carry over-range parameter values for a seam-crossing stretch; since a merely-`IsClosed()` (not necessarily `IsPeriodic()`) surface direction is not guaranteed to evaluate correctly at an out-of-range parameter (confirmed false for this round's own cylinder fixture - `ON_Cylinder::GetNurbForm()`'s standard clamped-knot circular form is closed but NOT periodic), the header's own documented caller contract is now explicit: reduce such a coordinate into the surface's own domain by whole periods before evaluating `S(u, v)` near a seam-crossing stretch (always valid for a closed direction, periodic or not). `out.uv` (the raw per-sample field) and `pulled_curve`'s own fit are unaffected - only `pcurve`'s own fit (and, via the shared chord-length `out.params`, `pulled_curve`'s parametrization) changes. Verified by `TestPullbackCurveToSurfaceAcrossPeriodicSeam` (tests/test_basic.cpp): a short arc of a cylinder's own base circle straddling its NURBS form's u=0/u=2*pi seam pulls back with `on_surface == true`; the RAW per-sample `uv` field still shows the wrapped-domain jump (confirming the test genuinely exercises the seam); the FITTED `pcurve`'s own u coordinate is monotonic end to end with no backward swing, and its total excursion matches the arc's actual 0.6 radian span, not a ~2*pi-0.6 "the long way around" detour; and, confirming the documented wrap-before-evaluate contract works, `pcurve`'s own two domain endpoints, reduced into the surface's domain, map back through the surface to the arc's own endpoints. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite re-run clean after a forced full rebuild (a background build earlier in this rotation started compiling the 60,000+-line `test_basic.cpp` before this second fix's own test had been written, silently linking a stale object file into an otherwise-green run - caught by grepping the built binary's own strings for the new tests' Check() messages before trusting that run, then fixed by touching sources and rebuilding clean): 8505 checks, 0 failures, 0 regressions (13 new checks this rotation - 9 for the periodic-seam pullback fix, 4 for face-interior self-intersection).

**2026-10-01, a further session on `kernel: Kernel-level data exchange`: one genuine correctness fix plus two genuine narrowings, no item flips.** (1) **A real pre-existing bug, found and fixed, not just disclosed:** every one of this file's n-gon (5+ corner) face loaders - `Mesh::LoadObj`/`LoadOff`/`LoadVrml`/`LoadCollada`/`LoadX3d`/`LoadUsda` (mesh.cpp) - used to fan-triangulate a face from its own first corner, each with its own copy of the identical disclosed caveat: "exact for a convex polygon; a concave one can produce a triangle whose interior falls outside the original face." That caveat is now closed, not just documented: a new shared `AppendPolygonFace()` helper (mesh.cpp, anonymous namespace) replaces every one of those six independent fan loops with a call to the SAME real ear-clipping triangulator `LoftClosedRings()`'s own end caps already use (`TriangulatePlanarRing()`, forward-declared earlier in the file so the loaders above it can call it too) - a concave n-gon's reflex corner can no longer produce a triangle poking outside the face, the exact failure mode the fan approach always had. Verified concretely, not just by construction: a new concave (reflex-cornered) hexagon fixture - `(4,0),(4,2),(2,2),(2,4),(0,4),(0,0)`, a 4x4 square with a 2x2 notch bitten out, true shoelace area 12 - is added to each of the six loaders' own existing `*FanTriangulatesNgonFaces` test functions (`TestMeshLoadObjFanTriangulatesNgonFaces` etc., tests/test_basic.cpp), fanned from this exact face's own first corner, (4,0); the OLD fan code on this fixture sums to 16, not 12 (the notch's own 2x2=4 area double-counted into an invalid triangle) - a concrete, worked counter-example that the new ear-clip code produces the correct 12 for, confirmed by each test's own area check. Because ear-clipping doesn't fan from a fixed first corner, it doesn't reproduce the OLD code's exact per-triangle corner assignment on existing CONVEX pentagon/hexagon fixtures either (the total area still matches - any valid triangulation of a simple polygon does - but which specific triangles are chosen differs), so each of the six tests' own hard-coded per-triangle index checks (asserting corners `(0,1,2)`/`(0,2,3)`/`(0,3,4)` specifically) no longer hold and are replaced with the pre-existing area-sum check alone; `TestMeshLoadObjFanTriangulatesNgonFaces`'s own separate relative-index (`-5 -4 -3 -2 -1`) sub-case, which used to assert the first triangle was literally `(0,1,2)`, now instead asserts the relative-index file's whole triangle list is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL to the absolute-index file's own (ear-clipping is a deterministic function of its input ring, so two files resolving to the same 0-based corners must triangulate identically) - a stronger equivalence check than the one triangle index it replaces. This closes the "OBJ read" bullet's own named fan-triangulation limitation outright, and narrows "Other mesh/scene exchange formats"' own identical disclosed limitation across the other five formats - see each bullet's own note below. (2) **Layouts:** `Model::AddLayout`/`LayoutCount`/`LayoutAt` (file_io.h; file_io.cpp) add a real Rhino page-space/"paper space" view - a plain `ON_3dmView` with `m_view_type` set to `ON::view_type::page_view_type` and `m_page_settings.m_width_mm`/`m_height_mm` carrying the page size, appended to `ON_3dmSettings::m_views` (OpenNURBS' own "current viewports" table, distinct from `AddNamedView()`'s own `m_named_views` table above) - the same "no Save()/Load() change needed, this table already round-trips through the settings chunk" situation `AddNamedView()` itself found. Closes the "layouts" half of the ".3dm attribute/metadata fidelity" bullet's own remaining "Still no textures/named views/lights/clipping planes/layouts/units" list (textures/named-views/lights/clipping-planes/units having each already closed in earlier sessions credited on that bullet below) - detail views (the viewport windows actually placed ON a layout, each framing part of model space at its own scale) are a separate, larger feature this pass does not attempt, so the bullet's own "layouts/details" item is only half-closed and stays `[partial]`. Verified by `TestModelAddLayoutRoundTrips` (tests/test_basic.cpp): the empty-name/non-positive-width/non-positive-height refusal cases, `LayoutAt()`'s exact name/page_width_mm/page_height_mm readback, an out-of-range `LayoutAt()` returning a default-constructed `LayoutInfo`, and two real layouts surviving an actual `.3dm` save/reload with their own distinct page sizes. (3) **Leader annotations:** `Model::AddLeader`/`LeaderCount`/`LeaderAt` (file_io.h; file_io.cpp) add this kernel's first `ON_Leader` support, built via `ON_Leader::Create(text, &ON_DimStyle::Default, point_count, points, plane, bWrapped=false, rect_width=0.0)` - the same "no dimstyle table of its own" narrowing `AddText()` already accepts, applied to a second `ON_Annotation` subtype. `LeaderAt()` converts `ON_Leader::Points2d()`'s own plane-local 2D storage back to the WORLD 3D points `AddLeader()` itself took in, via `plane.PointAt()`. Narrows "Rhino non-geometry/composite objects in .3dm"'s own disclosed "annotations besides plain ON_Text (dimensions, leaders)" gap to just dimensions - stays `[partial]`. Verified by `TestModelAddLeaderRoundTrips` (tests/test_basic.cpp): the empty-name/empty-text/degenerate-plane/too-few-points refusal cases, exact name/text/world-space-path-point readback, an out-of-range `LeaderAt()` returning a default-constructed `LeaderInfo`, and a real `.3dm` save/reload preserving the leader's text and every path point. **No item-classification change:** all four touched bullets (OBJ read; Other mesh/scene exchange formats; .3dm attribute/metadata fidelity; Rhino non-geometry/composite objects in .3dm) were already `[partial]` for their own other reasons (OBJ's own `.mtl`/per-group gap; SketchUp SKP; detail views; dimensions and `ON_HatchPattern`'s other fields, respectively) and stay `[partial]` - this category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts (10/13/4, 61.1%) and the Dino 8 kernel headline (69.6%) above are therefore unchanged by this pass. **2026-10-01, a fourth session on "Scripting, automation & visual programming" (app_scripting): Python's own interactive prompts are now real, not an architectural gap.** Both `Embedded Python 3` and `Python API breadth`'s own prior-session notes (below) named the same honest, repeatedly-deferred limitation: Python scripts ran start-to-finish in one call because CPython has no built-in way to suspend an arbitrary call stack and resume it later the way a Lua coroutine does for `rs.GetPoint`. This session builds that suspend/resume for real, on a worker thread rather than a coroutine - the second of the two approaches every prior note on this gap named as the honest way to close it, not attempted until now:

1. **The mechanism.** `PythonEngine::Start`/`StartFile`/`StartExpression` (`dino8-app/src/script/PythonEngine.{h,cpp}`) now launch the script on a dedicated `std::thread` (`ThreadMain`) and block the calling (UI) thread until that worker either finishes or suspends inside a new `dino8.GetPoint()`/`dino8.GetString()` call (`WaitForPoint`/`WaitForText`, called from the embedded module's new `GetPoint`/`GetString` bindings). Exactly one of the UI thread and the worker is ever runnable at a time - each `ResumePoint`/`ResumeText`/`ResumeNil`/`Abort` call wakes the worker and then blocks the caller again until the next suspend-or-finish, the same way `Start()` does - so there is no concurrent access to the Document or the Python interpreter despite the extra thread; it exists purely to get a real suspend point, not for parallelism. A genuine race was found and fixed during this session's own testing: the UI thread's wait has to require the worker to actually *consume* a resume (clearing its own handoff flag) before treating the still-stale "Suspended" state as a legitimate new answer, or a resumed script reads as "immediately re-suspended on the exact prompt it just answered" and gets wrongly cancelled (`WaitUntilSuspendedOrFinished`'s `!resume_ready_` guard, `PythonEngine.cpp`). `PythonEngine`'s constructor now releases the GIL once after `Py_Initialize()` (`PyEval_SaveThread`) so the worker thread can acquire it on demand via `PyGILState_Ensure`/`Release`, with an `atexit` hook restoring it to the finalizing thread immediately before the process-lifetime interpreter's own `Py_Finalize()` runs - missing this corrupted shutdown and segfaulted *every* run (caught by this session's own first full `smoke.sh` pass, not a flake, before being fixed and re-verified clean).
2. **Wiring it into the app.** `cmd_misc.cpp`'s `PythonScriptCommand` (`RunPythonScript`) and `ScriptCommand`'s own `.py`-dispatch branch (`RunScript`) both now pump a suspended Python script exactly the way they already pump a suspended Lua one - `OnPoint`/`OnText`/`OnEnter`/`OnCancel` route to `PythonEngine::ResumePoint`/`ResumeText`/`ResumeNil`/`Abort`. The Script Editor's Run button for a `.py` tab (`ui/Panels.cpp`) is rewired to go through `-RunPythonScript` (queuing the buffer the same way the Lua branch already queues through `-RunScript`) instead of calling `PythonEngine::Start` directly with no command context able to pump it, and its own Continue/"Waiting for input" indicator now reads Python's own `Running()`/`Suspended()` state for a loaded `.py` tab, not unconditionally Lua's.
3. **The compute server's own matching fix.** `main.cpp`'s `--serve` `/run/python` handler is updated to match: a `dino8.GetPoint()`/`dino8.GetString()` call there now genuinely *could* hang a synchronous HTTP connection the way `rs.GetPoint` already could (before this session, Python simply had no such function to call, so this was never a real risk), so the handler now checks `app.Python().Suspended()` after `Start()` returns and aborts with the same `500 "script requires interactive input"` response `/run`'s own Lua path already gives, instead of leaving a connection - and a blocked worker thread - open forever. `docs/COMPUTE_SERVER.md`'s "what this deliberately does not do" section is corrected to match (it previously claimed, now incorrectly, that Python had no `GetPoint`-style function to call at all).

Scope, stated honestly: only `GetPoint`/`GetString` are wired up this way - `rs.GetObjects`/`rs.GetReal`/`rs.GetInteger`-equivalents remain entirely unported, a real but now narrower gap than "no interactive prompts at all." The Windows-CPython-bundling half of "Embedded Python 3" is unchanged and still needs a packaging/installer change this session can't build or verify (no Windows runner here). Neither item's own `[partial]` classification flips to `[present]` - both are narrowed, not closed, this category's own established "close what you can verify, keep the rest honest" shape - so this category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts (11/3/1 of 15, 83.3%) and the Dino 8 headline above are unchanged by this pass.

Verified: `tests/smoke.sh`'s `python_script.txt` fixture now feeds `dino8.GetPoint()` and `dino8.GetString()` their answers as two further trailing script tokens on the same `RunPythonScript @TMP@/t.py 20,20,20 Widget2` line used to drive `RunPythonScript` itself (mirroring `script_script.txt`'s pre-existing `RunScript t.lua 20,20,20` for Lua) - the resumed script reads back the exact point and string the command line fed it and adds one new object, `@expect_objects` moving 36 → 37 to match. The `--serve` end-to-end section gains a sixth real HTTP request (`--serve-max-requests` 5 → 6): a `POST /run/python` calling the now-real `dino8.GetPoint()` is confirmed rejected the same way the pre-existing Lua `rs.GetPoint()` check already is, rather than hanging the connection - the exact regression this session's own `main.cpp` change above exists to prevent. Full `dino8-app` `ctest` suite (29/29) and the complete `tests/smoke.sh` (2176/2176 checks, 0 FAIL, 0 skip) both re-run clean on the merged branch after the race fix and the shutdown-crash fix above.

1. **Cloud/network compute service (Rhino.Compute equivalent)** — closes two more of the "what this deliberately does not do" gaps the item's own prior-session note named. (a) **Auth:** `net/ComputeServer.h`'s `HttpRequest` now carries every parsed request header (`TryParseHttpRequest`, lowercased name, RFC 7230-trimmed value — new header-parsing coverage in `tests/test_compute_server.cpp`), and `main.cpp`'s new `--serve-token TOKEN` flag checks it for a matching `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` header before a request's body ever reaches a script engine, answering `401 Unauthorized` otherwise — a real, if minimal, shared-secret check (compared with plain `==`, no hashing/rotation/per-caller tokens), not OAuth/API-key management; omitting the flag keeps the server exactly as open as before. Verified by 10 new `tests/smoke.sh` checks appended to `python_script.txt`'s existing scripted-QC fixture against a real build, round-tripping a set/get/erase cycle at both the per-object and document level. Still genuinely `[partial]`: interactive prompts (`GetPoint`/`GetObject`/`GetString`/etc.) remain entirely unported — porting those needs the same real architecture change (a coroutine-style suspend/resume CPython doesn't offer out of the box) every rotation on this item has deferred for the same honest reason; the Windows-CPython-bundling half of "Embedded Python 3" likewise needs a packaging/installer change this session can't build or verify (no Windows runner here) and was not attempted.

2. **Digital signing of exported files** moves `[missing]` -> `[present]`:
   no file-signing code existed anywhere before this. `dino8-app/src/io/
   DigitalSignature.h`/`.cpp` is a real RSA-2048/SHA-256/PKCS#1v1.5 file
   signature scheme - genuine asymmetric cryptography (the public key alone
   can verify but not forge a signature), not a checksum/HMAC - built
   entirely on a new from-scratch arbitrary-precision integer type
   (`dino8-app/src/util/BigUint.h`/`.cpp`: schoolbook add/sub/mul/divmod,
   binary modular exponentiation, and Miller-Rabin-tested prime generation)
   and the existing `util/Sha256.h`, no external crypto library. New
   `DigitalSign`/`VerifySignature` commands (`cmd_file.cpp`) sign any file
   with this machine's own signing key (generated once, on first use, at
   `<ConfigDirectory()>/signing_key.json`) and write/check a `.sig` sidecar.
   Verified against the classic textbook RSA worked example (p=61, q=53,
   e=17, d=2753 - independently hand-checkable), a full generated-keypair
   sign/verify round trip, and both failure paths a signature scheme exists
   to catch (a file edited after signing; the wrong public key) in a new
   standalone unit test (`dino8-app/tests/test_digital_signature.cpp`,
   ctest target `dino8_digital_signature`, 18/18 checks), plus end-to-end
   through the real app in `point_cloud_io_script.txt`/`smoke.sh` (sign,
   verify OK, change the file, verify now fails closed).
3. **IFC (BIM) import/export** moves `[missing]` -> `[present]`: nothing
   existed under the I/O sources before this. `dino8-app/src/io/
   FileIgesStep.{h,cpp}`'s new `ExportIfc`/`ImportIfc` write/read a real
   IFC4 file - the same ISO-10303-21 Part 21 physical-file syntax
   `ExportStep`/`ImportStep` already use (a new shared `ParseStepPhysicalFile`
   helper factors the generic Part-21 framing both readers need out of what
   was `ImportStep`-only code, with no behavior change to `ImportStep`
   itself), just IFC4's own entity vocabulary instead of AP214's. Honestly
   scoped like this codebase's other exchange formats: each exported object
   is tessellated to a mesh (`TessellateForIfc` - Breps/Surfaces/SubDs go
   through the same tessellation ExportPly already uses; Meshes as-is) and
   written as one `IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY` (a generic BIM element - Dino 8
   has no wall/door/beam classification to map onto IFC's real building-
   element types) with an `IFCTRIANGULATEDFACESET` shape, inside a minimal
   but complete `IFCPROJECT`/`IFCSITE`/`IFCBUILDING`/`IFCBUILDINGSTOREY`
   spatial hierarchy real IFC consumers expect to walk. Every `GlobalId` is
   a real, unique 22-character identifier from IFC's own GUID alphabet
   (`GenerateIfcGuid` - not a bit-for-bit implementation of buildingSMART's
   own UUID-compression algorithm, honestly noted as such in its own doc
   comment, but syntactically valid and collision-free, which is what an
   IFC reader actually relies on it for). **Verified against a real
   third-party IFC toolkit, not just this codebase's own reader**: installing
   IfcOpenShell and running its schema validator against a Dino 8-exported
   box found two real bugs during development (a `IfcGloballyUniqueId` whose
   first character wasn't restricted to '0'-'3', the real constraint a
   128-bit value compressed into 22 base-64 characters implies; and bare
   integer literals like `10` where ISO-10303-21 REAL attributes require a
   decimal point, e.g. `10.` - the latter a latent, previously-unnoticed
   strictness gap in the shared `Num()` formatter `ExportStep`'s own AP214
   output uses too, now fixed for both) - after both fixes, IfcOpenShell's
   validator reports zero errors and its geometry engine successfully
   extracts the exact tessellated mesh (vertex/triangle counts matching
   Dino 8's own export exactly). Also verified end-to-end through the real
   app (`dino8-app/tests/ifc_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): a Box exports and
   re-imports with its exact tessellated vertex/face count intact, and
   exporting a selection with nothing IFC-shaped (a bare point) fails
   cleanly instead of writing an empty/bogus file.

   the same Xvfb+llvmpipe recipe this document already treats as this

1. **`RunCommand` reported ambiguous command-name prefixes** —
   `CommandEngine::ResolveName` already resolved a prefix matching exactly
   one registered command (e.g. `Cir` -> `Circle`); a prefix matching
   *several* (e.g. `Pla`, which matches 12 registered commands - 11 catalog
   commands plus `Plane3Pt`, a `cmd_create.cpp` command with no
   `data/commands.json` catalog entry of its own) used to fall straight
   through to a flat `Unknown command: Pla`, leaving the user to guess or
   retype rather than see what it could mean. `RunCommand` now calls the
   same prefix-matching logic (factored out as `CommandEngine::
   PrefixMatches`) on a resolution failure and, when it finds more than one
   match, prints `Pla: ambiguous command name, could be: PlaceHole, Plan,
   Planar, ...` instead. A unique prefix and a genuinely unknown one
   (matching nothing at all) are both unchanged. This isn't a named gap
   anywhere in this document (Rhino's own ambiguous-prefix behavior was
   never scored here), so it doesn't itself move any item's status - a
   real command-system robustness fix, not a scored parity closure.
2. **Command aliases were invisible in the command-line autocomplete
   popup** - narrows the "Command aliases and shortcut customization"
   bullet below. The popup (`Application::DrawCommandLine`) only ever
   consulted `CommandCatalog::FuzzyMatch`, which knows nothing about
   `CommandEngine::Aliases()`: typing a default or user alias (e.g. `b` for
   `Box`, `di` for `Distance`) showed only catalog command matches - for a
   single-letter query like `b`, the shortest catalog command starting with
   `b` (`Box` itself) ranked first, so Down+Enter on the first row
   happened to run the right command, but with zero indication an alias
   existed, what it was bound to, or that typing it directly would have
   worked identically. A new `BuildAutocompleteRows` merges matching
   aliases (exact match first, then prefix, ahead of catalog fuzzy matches)
   into the popup with their own "Alias" badge and a "Alias for `<target>`"
   description; selecting one fills in the alias text itself, which
   `ResolveName` still resolves normally when it runs. Verified end-to-end
   (`tests/alias_autocomplete_script.txt`, driven through the real
   `@text`/`@key Down`/`@key Enter` popup interaction under Xvfb, the same
   mechanism `fuzzy_autocomplete_script.txt` already uses) - the check
   asserts the echoed command line reads `Command: b` (the alias text),
   not `Command: Box` (the old catalog-fallback result), so a regression
   back to the old behavior would be caught. Still doesn't touch the
   bullet's own named remaining gaps (the ~20 hardcoded reserved shortcuts
   a user binding still can't remap, the "type a key name" vs "press a
   key to capture" binding flow), so the item stays `[partial]`.
3. **`HistoryUpdate`, `HistoryPurge` and `SelObjectsWithHistory` were dead
   stubs, contradicting the real History mechanism right next to them** -
   directly closes the "History / associative re-execution" bullet's own
   named contradiction below. `cmd_history.cpp`'s real, working

   `"UpdateHistory"` - a name with no `data/commands.json` catalog entry of
   its own; the catalog's actual name for the same Rhino command,
   `HistoryUpdate`, was a separate `cmd_state.cpp` stub that always printed
   `HistoryUpdate: no construction history is recorded; nothing to update`
   regardless of what was genuinely tracked, so the real mechanism was
   unreachable under its own catalog identity. `HistoryPurge` (a

   `SelObjectsWithHistory` (a `cmd_select2.cpp` stub that always selected 0

   `HistoryUpdate` shares `UpdateHistory`'s rebuild via a common

   typed (`CommandEngine::ActiveName()`); `HistoryPurge` drops the
   recorded `HistoryRecord` for the current selection, or every tracked
   object in the document when nothing is selected; `SelObjectsWithHistory`
   selects every object `Document::FindHistoryRecord` still has a live
   entry for. Verified end-to-end against real recorded history, not just

**Another later same-day session's addition, in Blending & chamfering:**
closed PARITY_MAP's own "Alternative blend rail types (distance-from-edge,
distance-between-rails / disc blend, non-rolling-ball cross-section
placement)" gap - the ONE item this document had previously recorded as
`missing` in this category (see the "Alternative blend rail types" bullet
below, and the ranked-backlog row for the same item). Every fillet
elsewhere in `fillet.h`/`fillet.cpp` (`FilletConvexEdge`, `FilletConcaveEdge`,
and every function built on top of them) takes the rolling-ball RADIUS
directly as its one free parameter - Rhino 8's own `FilletEdge` command's
default `RailType=RollingBall`. Rhino 8 also exposes
`RailType=DistFromEdge` and `RailType=DistBetweenRails`: the exact same
rolling-ball fillet surface, specified by measuring a distance instead of a
radius. Four new functions add exactly that alternate input for the one
case this kernel's fillets are already exact on (a straight edge shared by
two PLANAR faces) - `FilletConvexEdgeByDistanceFromEdge`,
`FilletConvexEdgeByDistanceBetweenRails`, and their `FilletConcaveEdge`
mirrors (`dino8-kernel/include/dino8/kernel/fillet.h`,
`dino8-kernel/src/fillet.cpp`) - each a closed-form conversion to the
already-existing radius parameter, then a verbatim DISPATCH to
`FilletConvexEdge`/`FilletConcaveEdge`, not a re-implementation: both
functions' own `trim_back = radius / tan(theta / 2)` line (theta = the
edge's interior dihedral angle) is the classical wedge-incircle tangent-
length identity, inverted here (`radius = distance * tan(theta/2)` for
`DistFromEdge`) to pick out exactly the one circular arc a given rail
distance implies; `DistBetweenRails`'s own `radius = rail_distance /
(2*cos(theta/2))` is derived independently two ways in the header doc
comment (the wedge's own isosceles triangle, and directly from
`FilletConvexEdge`'s own `contact_i`/`contact_j` via
`|n_i - n_j| = 2*cos(theta/2)`), both agreeing.
Verified, not merely derived: five new tests in `tests/test_basic.cpp`
compare each new function's OUTPUT Brep against `FilletConvexEdge`/
`FilletConcaveEdge` called directly at an INDEPENDENTLY hand-derived
equivalent radius (topology, tessellated volume, and - for
`DistBetweenRails` - the literal 3D contact-point positions), on two
different dihedral angles: a box's own 90-degree edge (`theta=pi/2`, the
case where `DistFromEdge`'s own distance and the equivalent radius
coincide numerically - a necessary but not sufficient check on its own)
and a regular hexagonal prism's 120-degree side/side edge (`theta=2*pi/3`,
where `tan(theta/2) = sqrt(3)` genuinely exercises the formula rather than
hiding behind a `tan(45)=1` coincidence), plus the L-shaped concave prism's
own 90-degree reflex edge for the `FilletConcaveEdge` mirrors. A sixth new
test checks input validation: non-positive distances, a radius too large
to fit (propagated from the underlying `FilletConvexEdge`/
`FilletConcaveEdge` call, not re-implemented), a non-edge, and - genuinely
needed, not merely copied for symmetry, since `EdgeConvexity()` alone
cannot distinguish a convex edge from its concave mirror - feeding a
concave edge to a convex wrapper (and vice versa) is refused rather than
silently mis-dispatched. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite (4150+ checks) and
`ctest` both re-run clean afterward: 100% pass, 0 failures, 0 regressions.

**A later same-day session's addition, after this pass's own headline was
written:** kernel: Local / direct-edit operations gained a real
`PushPullFace(solid, face_index, distance)` (`boolean.h`/`boolean.cpp`),
closing PARITY_MAP's own "Push/pull a face (extrude face and merge/cut into
its own body)" gap — genuinely distinct from `OffsetFace`, which always
keeps a solid's face count fixed by re-extending/re-trimming every other
face in place. A **push** (`distance > 0`) leaves every other face
untouched and adds brand-new side-wall PlanarFaces (one per edge of the
pushed face's own loop) bridging the old boundary to the new one, plus a
new cap — genuinely extruded material, not a moved boundary (a box's top
face pushed out by 2 goes from 6 faces to 10, not OffsetFace's unchanged
6). A **pull** (`distance < 0`) instead retrims every neighbour face
whose own plane is perpendicular to the pushed face's normal, via a single
exact half-space clip (valid for a concave neighbour loop too), and adds no
new geometry — same net shape as an equivalent `OffsetFace` shrink, from a
completely different, boolean-free construction. This was **not** built by
extruding a NURBS profile via `Brep::Extrude()` and handing the result to
`BooleanCombinePlanar()`, the obvious first construction: that path was
tried and found to fail on two independent grounds, confirmed by testing,
not assumed — `Extrude()`'s own swept profile is only piecewise (not
globally) planar for a straight polygon, and even a hand-assembled
all-planar prism made `BooleanCombinePlanar()` throw ("an edge is shared by
3 or more faces") on the flush, zero-overlap coincident face a prism grown
directly off an existing face always has, a genuine gap in that engine's
own coincident-face handling. Direct topological surgery avoids both
problems entirely. Has **no convexity precondition** on `solid` at all
(unlike every other item already in this category), verified on both a box
and a genuinely non-convex, reflex-cornered L-shaped prism (push and pull
both), plus argument-error cases (zero distance, out-of-range face_index,
an oblique neighbour on a pull, a pull large enough to collapse a
neighbour) — five new tests in `tests/test_basic.cpp`, and the full
`dino8_kernel_tests` suite re-run clean (0 failures) after adding them.
Scoped to a planar-faced `solid` (`PlanarFaces()`'s own precondition, same
as every sibling in this category) and, for a pull, to neighbours
perpendicular to the pushed face (an oblique neighbour is refused, not
guessed at) — a curved-face push/pull and an oblique-neighbour pull remain
real, disclosed future work. This flips the item missing→partial: kernel:
Local/direct-edit operations moves from 6/17/5/28 (51.8%) to 6/18/4/28
(53.6%).

**Third same-day follow-up (this session):** kernel: Boolean operations
gained a genuine new kernel entry point, `SplitBySheet(solid, sheet)`
(boolean_general.h/.cpp) - the parity map's own next-highest-ranked still-
missing boolean item, "Sheet/solid trim (open surface as cutter through a
solid)". It reuses `BooleanCombineGeneral`'s/`ImprintFaces`' own SSX-
gathering and `FragmentFaces()` machinery for both operands, but - unlike
either of those - only ONE operand (`solid`) is required to be closed:
`solid`'s own fragments are bucketed by a new closest-point-plus-normal-
sign test (`ClassifySideOfSheet`, using the existing Newton-polished
`SurfaceClosestPointGlobal`) against `sheet`, which may be a genuinely open
cutting surface with no volume to ray-cast in/out of at all; `sheet`'s own
fragments are ray-cast in/out of `solid` as usual (valid since `solid`
really is closed) and its IN fragments become a new, correctly-oriented
cap face added to BOTH output pieces. Modeled on boolean.cpp's own
`SplitByPlane` (returns both pieces rather than one caller-chosen "kept"
side, since which piece to keep is a UI decision, not a geometric one).
Verified (`TestSplitBySheet*`, tests/test_basic.cpp): a 4x4x4 box fully
severed by a flat open planar sheet larger than the box's own footprint
comes back as two valid closed B-reps whose volumes are each exactly half
(32) and sum back to the original (64) exactly; a sheet that never
reaches the solid at all correctly returns the whole untouched solid on
one side and the empty Brep on the other, mirroring `ImprintFaces`' own
"kept.empty()" convention; both faceless-operand cases throw
`std::invalid_argument`. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite (via `ctest`):
100% passing, 0 regressions.

Still `partial`, not `present`: no app command exposes it yet
(`cmd_boolean.cpp` still skips every non-closed operand outright); it
inherits `BooleanCombineGeneral`'s own scope limits (one crossing chain
per opposing face pair, genus-0 faces); only a flat cutting plane is
tested (a genuinely curved `sheet` is unexercised); and the item's OTHER
half - trimming a sheet body BY a solid (cutting the sheet's own surface
down, not splitting a volume) - is not implemented at all. Net effect on
the scores below: kernel: Boolean operations' "Sheet/solid trim" bullet
upgrades missing -> partial: 8/15/2/25 (62.0%, was 8/14/3/25 60.0%);
weighted the same marginal-delta way as the two follow-ups above (this
row's own weight of 1.5 against the 17.75 total kernel weight, on top of
the 64.6% those two already established, not a full re-derivation of
every other row): 64.6% → 64.8%.

**Sixth same-day follow-up (a parallel session):** kernel: Boolean operations' own
`BooleanCombineGeneral(a, b, op, tolerance)` (boolean_general.h/.cpp) now
takes an optional caller-specified `tolerance` — until now every entry
point in that file (`BooleanCombineGeneral`, `ImprintFaces`, `SplitBySheet`)
default-constructed its own internal `IntersectOptions` with no way for a
caller to loosen or tighten the SSX Newton-refinement accuracy at all.
Defaults to the prior implicit 0.001, so every existing caller is
bit-for-bit unaffected — verified directly (`TestBooleanCombineGeneral
CallerTolerance`, tests/test_basic.cpp): omitting the parameter reproduces
identical topology (face/edge counts) and a bit-identical tessellated
volume to passing the explicit prior default. The parameter is a genuine,
wired-through control, not a decorative no-op: on the box+cylinder
Intersection fixture (the same fixture `TestBooleanCombineGeneralBox
Cylinder` uses), whose result is entirely two SSX-computed circles where
the box's top/bottom planes cut the cylinder wall, a tight tolerance
(1e-7) keeps every result vertex within 1e-4 of the true cylinder radius
while a loose one (0.05) measurably degrades that same measurement by
more than 10x — a real, direct measurement of the actual Newton-refinement
solve accuracy, not tessellation density (this engine's edges are built
one straight `ON_LineCurve` segment at a time between consecutive
Newton-refined chain/vertex points, so the brep's own vertices are exactly
where that accuracy shows up). A non-positive tolerance now throws
`std::invalid_argument`, the same typed-refusal convention this file
already uses for `SymmetricDifference`/faceless operands. Full
`dino8_kernel_tests` suite (via `ctest`): 100% passing, 0 regressions.

**Sixth same-day follow-up (a parallel session):** three of the five named sub-operators in
**Kernel: SubD & mesh kernel support**'s own "Kernel-native SubD local
edit operators (insert edge, extrude face, spin edge, weld, expand)"
[missing] item now genuinely exist: `SubD::InsertEdge`, `SubD::SpinEdge`,
and `SubD::ExtrudeFace` (dino8-kernel/src/subd.cpp, dino8-kernel/include/
dino8/kernel/subd.h). Each is a thin, validated wrapper around a real
(read directly, not assumed non-stub) OpenNURBS primitive this kernel had
never called before: `ON_SubD::SplitFace(face, v0, v1)` for InsertEdge
(divides a face into two along a new edge between two of its own
non-adjacent corners), `ON_SubD::SpinEdge(edge, spin_clockwise)` for
SpinEdge (rotates a shared interior edge's endpoints around its two
adjacent faces' boundaries - the SubD analog of a triangle mesh's
edge-flip), and `ON_SubD::ExtrudeComponents(xform, cptr_list, 1)` for
ExtrudeFace (translates one face along its own outward
`ControlNetCenterNormal()`, genuinely opening a "chimney" through side
faces rather than detaching a floating island, when the extruded face
already had neighbors). All three follow this class's existing point-pair
vertex lookup convention (`FindVertex`/`FindEdge`, matching
`SetCrease`/`SetEdgeSharpness`/`CapBoundaryLoop`) rather than inventing a
new one.

Verified with 3 new tests (`TestSubDInsertEdgeSplitsFaceIntoTwoAlongDiagonal`,
`TestSubDSpinEdgeRotatesSharedInteriorEdge`,
`TestSubDExtrudeFaceAddsProtrusionAlongNormal`, tests/test_basic.cpp): a
lone flat quad splits along its diagonal into exactly two genuine
triangles (1/4/4 → 2/4/5 face/vertex/edge counts) and refuses to re-split
an already-adjacent pair or a pair no longer sharing a big-enough face;
the shared interior edge of a two-quad strip genuinely changes which
vertex pair it connects (checked by id, not just by the boolean return
value) while every topology count and `Check()`'s manifold-single-body
verdict stay exactly the same, and a naked boundary edge or an unknown
point both correctly refuse; and a lone free-standing quad extruded along
its own normal comes back as 5 faces / 8 vertices / 12 edges with the
moved face's own 4 corners landing exactly at +distance and 4 brand-new
vertices left behind at the original (now open, per `Check()`'s
`naked_edges == 4`) footprint - a real protrusion, not a floating
disconnected copy. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite (via `ctest`): 100%
passing, 0 regressions.

Still `partial`, not `present`: the other two named sub-operators, weld
(joining two separate edges/vertices together) and expand (a uniform
push-apart of a face/region), have no kernel entry point at all still;
`InsertEdge` only splits a quad-or-larger face along two of ITS OWN

dino8-kernel/include/dino8/kernel/subd.h) closes the fourth of the five
named sub-operators in this category's own "Kernel-native SubD local edit
operators (insert edge, extrude face, spin edge, weld, expand)" item -
"expand" (the Sixth follow-up's own text: "a uniform push-apart of a
face/region").

`ExpandFaces(face_ids, distance)` delegates to the exact same real,
non-stub `ON_SubD::ExtrudeComponents(xform, cptr_list, cptr_count)`
primitive `ExtrudeFace()` already uses, but calls it with EVERY face in
`face_ids` as one component list and a single shared translation, instead
of looping `ExtrudeFace()` once per face. That distinction is the entire
point of "expand a region" versus "extrude each face separately": reading
`ON_SubD::Internal_ExtrudeComponents` directly (opennurbs_subd.cpp:23265
onward, in the fetched `opennurbs-src` build dependency) confirms its own
component-marking pass extrudes an edge only when it is attached to
exactly one marked face, or is already a boundary edge - an edge attached
to TWO marked faces (i.e. shared between two faces both being expanded
together) is left alone. So a multi-face region moves as one rigid block,
opening exactly one ring of new side faces around its own outer boundary,
while every edge interior to the region stays interior and unwalled -
genuine ON_SubD behavior this wrapper exposes, not something it
implements itself. The push direction is the unit-vector sum of each
listed face's own `ControlNetCenterNormal()` (each unitized before
summing, the sum itself unitized), the natural multi-face generalization
of `ExtrudeFace()`'s own single-face normal convention, refusing rather
than guessing when that sum is degenerate (e.g. two faces with exactly
opposite normals cancel).

Verified with 3 new tests (tests/test_basic.cpp):
`TestSubDExpandFacesSingleFaceMatchesExtrudeFace` confirms a one-face
region reproduces `ExtrudeFace()`'s own exact topology delta on the
identical lone-quad fixture (1/4/4 -> 5/8/12 face/vertex/edge counts, all
corners moved to the requested distance) bit-for-bit, plus this method's
own extra argument-refusal cases (empty list, a duplicate face id).
`TestSubDExpandFacesMovesConnectedRegionAsOneBlockKeepingSharedEdgeInterior`
expands the two-quad strip fixture `TestSubDSpinEdgeRotatesSharedInteriorEdge`
already uses (2 faces sharing one interior edge) as a single region and
checks, by edge id, that the shared edge is STILL `HasInteriorEdgeTopology`
(exactly 2 faces) afterward, with both its own endpoints moved to the
requested distance along with the rest of the region - not walled off into
two independent protrusions - while the resulting face/vertex/edge counts
(2/6/7 -> 8/12/19) and `Check()`'s naked-edge count (6, exactly the
region's own new open base) match hand-derived expectations for a single
combined extrude, not the larger count two independent single-face
extrudes on the same shared edge would produce.
`TestSubDExpandFacesRefusesWhenRegionNormalsCancel` builds two disjoint,
oppositely-wound freestanding quads (unit normals (0,0,1) and (0,0,-1))
and confirms `ExpandFaces` refuses the pair (their sum is the zero vector,
no well-defined single push direction) and leaves the SubD completely
unchanged. Full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite re-run via `ctest`: 100%
passing, 0 regressions.

through shared vertices — the wire-body analogue of

share one vertex" convention, applied to wire topology instead of face
loops. `IsWireBody()` is the structural query counterpart (at least one
live edge, zero live faces). Confirmed by direct measurement, not assumed:

zero-face Brep — `GroupVertexEdgesByFace()`'s own "0 for a vertex that
touches no live face at all" case (already documented, previously
exercised only via a wire edge hanging off an otherwise-solid vertex) means
a wire body's own vertices never trip `NonManifoldVertex`, and the
face-indexed loops in `Check()` simply iterate zero times.
