**SubD symmetry/mirror-in-place** — `Symmetrize()`'s own disclosed
   remaining gap: "a vertex that starts strictly off-plane is always
   duplicated (never welded to a same-side neighbor)." The single
   `point_tolerance` argument did double duty - both classifying which
   vertices sit ON the mirror plane (correctness-sensitive: loosening it
   can silently change which boundary loop gets welded as a seam) AND
   bounding `ON_SubD::FindOrAddVertex`'s own position-match weld for
   every mirrored vertex - so there was no way to weld two genuinely-
   distinct-but-nearly-coincident off-plane vertices (e.g. two
   independently-modeled features meant to share a seam that drifted
   apart at single-float `ON_3fPoint` precision) without also loosening
   on-plane classification. `SubD::Symmetrize()` (subd.cpp:321,
   subd.h:507) now takes an optional `weld_tolerance` parameter (default
   `0.0`, meaning "reuse `point_tolerance`," exactly as before this
   parameter existed): when positive, it is used instead of
   `point_tolerance` for every `FindOrAddVertex` lookup, on-plane and
   off-plane alike (harmless for the on-plane case, whose target position
   is already exactly the original vertex's own point, so a looser search
   there still only ever finds that same vertex). Verified by
   `TestSubDSymmetrizeWeldsNearDuplicateOffPlaneVerticesWithExplicitWeldTolerance`
   (tests/test_basic.cpp): two off-plane quads built as entirely separate
   vertex records, identical except for a 1e-4 x-shift (far bigger than
   the tight 1e-9 default, modeling realistic float drift between two
   "same" features), stay 8 distinct vertices after `FromControlMesh()`
   (sanity: not silently merged by construction); mirroring at the
   default tolerance produces 16 vertices total - the mirrored
   near-duplicate pair stays just as unwelded as the original pair,
   reproducing the disclosed gap exactly, byte-identical to this
   method's behavior before `weld_tolerance` existed; mirroring with
   `weld_tolerance = 1e-3` instead produces 12 - the mirrored pair welds
   into one vertex, while the ORIGINAL pair (never touched by
   `Symmetrize()`, which only ever processes vertices it is itself
   mirroring) stays unwelded, confirming the fix is scoped to exactly the
   vertices it claims to affect. Still honestly `[partial]`: this is not
   a general "weld any two nearby vertices" tool - a duplicate already
   present in the ORIGINAL half before `Symmetrize()` runs is untouched,
   the same scope limit `SubD::Check()`'s own duplicate-vertex disclosure
   already names (SubD has no `Mesh::MergeDuplicateVertices()`
   counterpart) - and live constrained symmetric editing remains
   out of scope, unchanged.

Kept at `[partial]`: Sweep2, NetworkSrf's 3-curve case and Patch's non-planar case are all exactly as limited as before - this closes one sub-gap of several the bullet names, not the bullet itself. **A later pass closes the Sweep2 half named above:** `Sweep2Command`'s single-cross-section case (`cmd_surface.cpp`'s `Build`) now calls the kernel's own exact `Brep::Sweep2` (`RebuildSweep2`, `history_rebuild.h`/`cmd_surface.cpp`) the same way Sweep1's own single-section case already does, instead of this file's own scaled-frame-and-fit construction between the two rails. Verified end-to-end: `surface_script.txt`'s existing two-straight-rails/single-line-section case now reads `Sweep2: exact kernel sweep (two-rail frame transport)` in place of the old `"1 section(s) along 2 rail stations"` message. Kept at `[partial]`: Sweep2's multi-section case, NetworkSrf's 3-curve case and Patch's non-planar case are all exactly as limited as before.
- [partial] Solid editing with B-rep results (booleans, fillet, shell, offset) — BooleanUnion/Difference/Intersection convert every operand to a mesh before combining (`dino8-app/src/commands/cmd_boolean.cpp:1`, "Boolean and splitting commands (mesh-based, via Manifold)"); the kernel's exact `BooleanCombineMixed` is never called from the app. FilletEdge is exact only when both adjacent faces are planar, else a mesh fallback. Shell, OffsetSrf on polysurfaces, and Pipe Cap=Yes all give meshes. New this window: `SplitByObjectCommand` (`cmd_boolean.cpp:290`) adds a general cutting-solid/surface split, but it is the same mesh-boolean pattern — its own status line literally prints "mesh boolean; results are meshes" (`cmd_boolean.cpp:386`) — so it reinforces rather than changes this bullet's partial status. (A same-day follow-up, commit 167baae, fixed the command silently deleting its cutter and re-meshing the target with zero real effect when the cutter merely missed or fully enclosed the target — a correctness fix, not a capability change; see kernel: Transformations for detail.) Solid primitives themselves are real Breps. **Correction (this pass):** the "BooleanUnion/Difference/Intersection convert every operand to a mesh before combining" half of the clause above is stale, not current — it predates **kernel: Boolean operations**'s own "B-rep-preserving booleans reachable from the application" bullet's "Twelfth note" (`TryExactBrepBoolean`, the shared helper `BooleanUnion`/`BooleanDifference`/`BooleanIntersection`/`Boolean2Objects` all now call first, dino8-app/src/commands/cmd_boolean.cpp, `BooleanCombinePlanarNAry`), which now also has its compound-operand support verified end-to-end (this same pass). The "the kernel's exact `BooleanCombineMixed` is never called from the app" half remains true and current, not stale — wiring it in as a second attempt (for an operand with a cylindrical face) was tried and reverted this same pass, after finding it can silently accept adversarial geometry the planar engine correctly refuses, and that a record-less operand's own result doesn't tessellate closed via the app's own generic mesh path (see that same bullet's own "A later pass" account for the full detail, including the real, narrower `MixedFaces()` kernel bug this investigation did fix). This item's own `partial` classification is unaffected (FilletEdge/Shell/OffsetSrf/Pipe remain exactly as described) - narrows, does not flip, the same already-partial item. **A later pass narrows the Shell half named above, the plain fully-closed case only:** `ShellCommand`'s plain case (no face clicked to remove/open, no per-face thickness override - `cmd_surface.cpp`'s `OnNumber`) now tries the kernel's own exact `ShellConvexPlanar` first, giving a real Brep result (`SceneObject::MakeBrep`, not a tessellated mesh) for any solid whose faces are all planar and whose shape is convex - a box or other simple polyhedron - before falling back to the existing mesh construction (outer minus inward vertex-normal offset) the same "exact first, fail open" shape `TryExactBrepBoolean` already uses for the booleans; a curved face, non-convex shape, or a thickness beyond that shape's own offset feasibility still falls straight through to the mesh path unchanged. `ShellConvexPlanar` itself had zero callers anywhere in `dino8-app/src` before this, closing exactly the gap this bullet's own wording named. One disclosed wrinkle: `Brep::Volume()` refuses every face `ShellConvexPlanar` builds (even a plain rectangle) as "trimmed" (`Brep::FromPlanarFaces()`'s own general construction, not specific to this caller), so the printed volume is read from the same display-mesh tessellation (`MeshOf`) the app already uses for rendering - the figure printed is therefore approximate in the same sense any displayed mesh is, but the object actually stored is the exact Brep. Verified end-to-end: `surface_script.txt`'s existing 20x20x10-box Shell case now reads `Shell: thickness 1, closed, exact B-rep, volume 1408` (the same exact 1408 as before, now from a real B-rep), confirmed by `SelPolysrf` (not the old `SelClosedMesh`) selecting the result. Kept at `[partial]`: Shell's own face-removed/per-face-override/non-convex/curved-face cases, `BooleanCombineMixed`, FilletEdge's non-planar case, OffsetSrf on polysurfaces and Pipe Cap=Yes are all exactly as limited as before - this closes one sub-gap of several the bullet names, not the bullet itself.
- [partial] History / associative re-execution — real History/RecordHistory/UpdateHistory exist (`cmd_history.cpp`, `cmd_misc.cpp`, `cmd_solids.cpp`), but only for Extrude, ExtrudeCrvToPoint, Revolve, Loft and SubDLoft. **Corrected this pass:** the "stale stubs elsewhere in the app still print 'no construction history is recorded', contradicting the real mechanism" half of this bullet is fixed, not merely narrowed. `HistoryUpdate` (the catalog's real name - `cmd_history.cpp`'s working rebuild had only ever been registered as `UpdateHistory`, a name with no `data/commands.json` entry of its own, so the real mechanism was unreachable under its own catalog identity), `HistoryPurge` and `SelObjectsWithHistory` were all dead `cmd_state.cpp`/`cmd_select2.cpp` stubs that always claimed no history was recorded or selected 0 objects outright, regardless of what was genuinely tracked. All three now check `Document::HistoryRecords()`/`FindHistoryRecord()` for real: `HistoryUpdate` shares `UpdateHistory`'s rebuild; `HistoryPurge` drops recorded history for the selection (or the whole document with nothing selected); `SelObjectsWithHistory` selects every object with a live record. Verified against real recorded history, not just the empty-document case (`tests/history_purge_script.txt`). **A further pass adds a sixth tracked command, Pipe:** `PipeCommand::OnNumber` (`cmd_surface.cpp`) now retains each rail curve's `ObjectId` (previously only a plain `kernel::NurbsCurve` copy via `CurvesOf`, with no id to record) and calls the new free `RebuildPipe` (declared in `history_rebuild.h`, defined in `cmd_surface.cpp` after its file's anonymous namespace closes so it has external linkage for `cmd_history.cpp` to call, while still reaching that namespace's own `ArcLengthParams`/`RmfFrames`/`MeshFromRows`/`SurfaceFromRows`/`Outward`/`kRailSamples`/`kRingSegments` helpers by ordinary unqualified lookup) - the exact same construction the live command itself now delegates to, reproducing radius, Cap=Yes/No, and the open-surface case's CV-circle radius correction from `rec.num` alone, with `wrap` (closed rail, and so mesh-vs-surface) read fresh from whichever curve is passed in rather than recorded, so a rail opened/closed since the pipe was built is honoured on rebuild. `RebuildOneHistoryObject` (`cmd_history.cpp`) dispatches `rec.command == "Pipe"` to it and also re-calls `Document::SetPipeFeature` with the curve's current geometry, keeping that separate side-table tag (`ExtractPipedCurve`'s own source) in sync too - without this, PipeFeature would keep pointing at the rail's geometry from whenever the pipe was first built, stale the same way the object's own SceneObject geometry would be without `ReplaceGeometry`. Verified end-to-end (`tests/history_pipe_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`) with the same real-bounding-box-move money check as the original five commands: a radius-1 capped pipe around a line, History On, reads `min 0,-1,-1 max 10,1,1`; after moving the line 5 units in +Z and running UpdateHistory, it reads `min 0,-1,4 max 10,1,6` - genuinely re-derived, not a stale bake. **This pass adds a seventh tracked command, Sweep1's single-cross-section case:** now that `Sweep1Command`'s single-profile case calls the kernel's exact `Brep::Sweep1` (see "Surface construction commands" above for the construction change itself), it is deterministic from its two source curves alone, so it fits the same record-and-rebuild shape - `Sweep1Command::Build` (`cmd_surface.cpp`) keeps both the rail's and the section's `ObjectId` and records `{rail_id, section_id}` as `rec.sources`; `RebuildOneHistoryObject` (`cmd_history.cpp`) dispatches `rec.command == "Sweep1"` to the same `RebuildSweep1` the live command itself calls, re-fetching both sources' *current* geometry. One real wrinkle surfaced and is disclosed honestly rather than glossed over: `Brep::Sweep1` carries the section RIGIDLY along the rail, preserving its offset from the rail's own current start point - so a pure translation of the RAIL alone, with the section left in place, exactly cancels out in the rebuilt result (the recomputed offset absorbs the rail's own shift), unlike Pipe's or Extrude's source-curve-moves check. The verification fixture (`tests/history_sweep1_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`) therefore moves the *section* curve instead (still a real bounding-box-move money check, not just an object count): a radius-1 circle swept up a 10-unit vertical line reads `min -0.9073,-0.978,0 max 1,0.978,10` (the x/y mins fall a little short of the circle's true -1 - a display-tessellation artifact of the `BoundingBox` command's own meshing, not the underlying exact geometry); after moving the circle 5 units in +Z and running UpdateHistory, the whole tube reads `min -0.9073,-0.978,5 max 1,0.978,15` - genuinely re-derived. The item's own remaining scope limit - only those seven construction commands ever record history at all, and Sweep1 only in its single-section case - is unchanged, so it stays `[partial]`. **This pass adds an eighth tracked command, Sweep2's single-cross-section case:** now that `Sweep2Command`'s single-profile case calls the kernel's exact `Brep::Sweep2` (see "Surface construction commands" above for the construction change itself), it is deterministic from its two rails plus one section curve, so it fits the same record-and-rebuild shape - `Sweep2Command::Build` (`cmd_surface.cpp`) keeps both rails' and the section's `ObjectId` and records `{rail1_id, rail2_id, section_id}` as `rec.sources`; `RebuildOneHistoryObject` (`cmd_history.cpp`) dispatches `rec.command == "Sweep2"` to the same `RebuildSweep2` the live command itself calls, re-fetching all three sources' *current* geometry. The verification fixture (`tests/history_sweep2_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`) uses two parallel vertical rails and a radius-1 circle section, and moves the *section* curve (not a rail) for the same cancellation reason Sweep1's own fixture does: a fresh build reads `min -0.9073,-0.978,0 max 1,0.978,10` (identical to Sweep1's own straight-rail case, since the constant rail-to-rail width cancels out the two-rail scaling); after moving the section 5 units in +Z and running UpdateHistory, the whole tube reads `min -0.9073,-0.978,5 max 1,0.978,15` - genuinely re-derived. The item's own remaining scope limit - only those eight construction commands ever record history at all, and Sweep1/Sweep2 only in their single-section case - is unchanged, so it stays `[partial]`.
- [partial] Command-level feature editing (re-running a construction with new inputs) — only scoped, explicit-recompute mechanisms exist (UpdateHistory, hole features, a few UpdateDimensions/UpdateBakes commands); no universal parametric feature tree.
- [partial] VBA-style macro recorder and editor — a macro editor does exist (`dino8-app/src/ui/Panels.cpp:1606` `DrawMacroEditor`, a multi-line panel with Run/Copy, `;`-separated command sequences, command-file playback, plus a Lua/Python script editor). **New this pass: the persistence half of the gap is closed.** The macro buffer moved out of a function-local `static char[4096]` into `AppState::macro_text` (`Application.h`, alongside `working_folder`/`startup_script`) and now round-trips through `Settings.cpp`'s own `"macro_text"` key the same as every other Option — survives an app restart (`LoadSettings`/`SaveSettings`, called from `Application::Init`/`Shutdown`) and an explicit `OptionsExport`/`OptionsImport`, not just for the life of one open panel. **A further pass closes half of the remaining gap: a real action recorder now exists**, scoped to typed command lines. `AppState::macro_recording` (`Application.h`) gates a new hook in `CommandEngine::Execute` (`CommandEngine.cpp`): while on, every top-level typed command line (`input`, the exact text as typed, args included - not a nested/deferred line from inside a running Macro/script, and not `RecordMacro` itself, so toggling recording off never leaves a trailing "RecordMacro Off" as the buffer's own last line) is appended verbatim to `AppState::macro_text`, the same buffer Run/Copy/persistence already use. `RecordMacro` (`cmd_misc.cpp`, a new custom command - no Rhino catalog entry by this name) is the On/Off toggle, same report-or-set shape as History/RecordHistory (`cmd_history.cpp`'s `ToggleOrReport`): with no argument it now also dumps the buffer's current contents line by line, so a recorded session can be inspected/verified from the command line or a script, not only by opening the Macro Editor panel. The Macro Editor panel (`Panels.cpp`'s `DrawMacroEditor`) gained a matching Record/"Recording... (click to stop)" toggle button next to Run/Copy, going through `Execute("RecordMacro On/Off")` rather than poking the flag directly so the command-line feedback and the button's own label never disagree. Verified end-to-end (`tests/record_macro_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): typed lines while On land in the buffer in order; a line typed after Off does not; `RecordMacro` never records itself. Scope, stated honestly: this observes typed command LINES, the same unit Rhino's own command-line macro recording captures - not raw mouse clicks, viewport picks, or panel interactions with no command-line equivalent, and any VBA/object-model compatibility remains entirely absent - the buffer is still a plain `;`-free, one-command-per-line text box, not a recorded, editable macro object with properties. Stays `[partial]`.
- [missing] AutoLISP-equivalent command scripting language — no LISP dialect or AutoLISP compatibility anywhere; scripting is Lua, Python or Macro/command files.
- [missing] ObjectARX-equivalent native extension API — the only native API is a Dino-specific plugin ABI, not an ObjectARX-compatible binary interface.

**Dino 8: 2D drafting, annotation & documentation** (app_drafting):
- [partial] Associative annotation updating (dimensions, leaders, center marks, center lines) — UpdateDimensions rebuilds several dimension/leader/mark types from their anchors, but only on an explicit command run, and a point is anchored only if it coincides exactly with a Point object or curve endpoint. Earlier windows extended the same explicit-recompute shape to MultiLeader arrows (`UpdateMultiLeaders`, commit `0ebdb07`), the four GD&T symbol commands (`UpdateGdtSymbols`, commit `f66cdf9`), for the electrical vertical-market toolset (elec/ElecComponents.h), PanelSchedule's rows when built from a real ElecCircuit-tagged component selection rather than hand-typed Circuits= text (`UpdatePanelSchedule`, commit `bb673bb`) — the same BomAll/BomRefIds-style all-vs-explicit-selection split BillOfMaterials already used — and TitleBlock's Name field (`UpdateTitleBlock`, commit `dfee1cf`), which tracks the document's own Settings().title (Document Properties) unless frozen by an explicit Name=. This window adds a fourth family, the whole-object-reference measured dimensions from cmd_annotate2.cpp: DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume (`MeasureRefIds`, a BomRefIds-style id list, since these can sum several selected objects) and DimCreaseAngle (`DimRefObj1`/`DimRefObj2`, two objects directly, same whole-object-reference shape DimRadius/DimDiameter and CenterLine already use) are now associative via a new `UpdateMeasureDims` command: it re-measures each recorded object's *current* shape (not just its position — an edited curve's new length, a resized solid's new volume, a re-pointed line's new direction all propagate), sums/recombines exactly as the creating command did, and rebuilds the leader in place at its original landing point, dropping a since-deleted or no-longer-measurable object from the result the same way BillOfMaterials's BomRefIds drops a deleted one. A dimension built before this window carries no MeasureRefIds/DimRefObj1 tag and stays a static baked measurement, same as before. This window closes two more of the family's remaining gaps. DimOrdinate (base point + feature points) is now associative per point exactly like DimLinear: `FindPointAnchor` matches the base point once and, separately, each feature point against a real Point object or curve endpoint, and `UpdateMeasureDims` (extended to cover it, same command DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume/DimCreaseAngle use) re-evaluates whichever matched and redraws that ordinate's leader/text from their current positions — a point that was never anchored still redraws from its built DimP0/DimP1 fallback, unchanged, rather than being skipped. TitleBlock's Date field now works the same way its Name field already did: left unset it defaults to (and stays tagged associative to, `TitleBlockDateAuto`) today's date, and `UpdateTitleBlock` re-pulls it independently of Name — an explicit Date= freezes just that field, same as an explicit Name= freezes Name. Scale/Sheet (TitleBlock) still have no associative mechanism — Sheet's default is merely which layout happened to be active when the title block was placed, not a stable property (Layout has no id, only a name) the table could track back to. This window fixes a correctness gap in the associativity machinery itself rather than adding a new family: `DimTolerance` (cmd_drafting2.cpp) appends a tolerance suffix to a dimension's baked text, but `UpdateDimensions`/`UpdateMeasureDims` rebuild that text from scratch (the freshly recomputed measurement alone), so a tolerance added to an otherwise-associative dimension — DimLinear/DimAligned, DimAngle, DimRadius/DimDiameter, DimOrdinate, DimArea/DimCurveLength/DimVolume, DimCreaseAngle — used to vanish silently the next time its anchor moved and the dimension was regenerated. It is now recovered from the `DimTolerance.Base` tag `DimTolerance` itself leaves (diffed against the pre-rebuild text to get the suffix) and re-appended to the freshly rebuilt measurement (`GroupToleranceSuffix`/`ReapplyToleranceSuffix`, annotate_common.h, shared by both Update commands) — re-running Update after moving the measured geometry now keeps the tolerance, not just re-running DimTolerance's own idempotent re-apply. Leader was already unaffected (its text is a static label copied verbatim on rebuild, never recomputed) and Centermark/CenterLine have no text to lose. This window widens the anchor-matching mechanism itself (`FindPointAnchor`/`ResolveAnchor`, annotate_common.h) rather than adding another dimension family: a measured point used to associate only when it coincided exactly with a Point object or a curve's start/end (the literal limit this bullet's opening sentence names); it now also recognizes a curve's segment midpoint (a degree-1/polyline curve — one candidate per segment, so an interior segment's own midpoint anchors, not just the first) or arc-length midpoint (any higher-degree curve), and an arc/circle's center or, for a full circle, one of its four quadrant points (+x/-x/+y/-y around its own plane) — the exact same candidate points the viewport's own Mid/Cen/Quad object snaps already compute (`Viewport.cpp`), so a point picked with one of those snaps now resolves to a live anchor instead of silently staying a static bake. Every `FindPointAnchor`/`ResolveAnchor` consumer gets this for free, with no per-command change needed: DimLinear/DimAligned/DimRotated's two points, DimAngle's vertex and two direction points, DimOrdinate's base and feature points, Leader's and MultiLeader's arrow tips, and FeatureControlFrame/DatumFeature/SurfaceFinish/WeldSymbol's feature points. A point resolved only by a snap this build still has no anchor code for at all (Near, Perp, Tangent, Knot, a brep vertex, ...) stays a static baked measurement, same as before. More annotation/table types now re-associate, an earlier same-day window made DimTolerance correct under rebuild, and this window widens the point-anchor mechanism itself across the whole family, but the underlying gap this bullet names (no automatic recompute hooked into document edits) is unchanged, so it stays partial. A later window widens `FindPointAnchor`/`ResolveAnchor` again, closing two more of the anchor kinds the curve-midpoint/arc-center/quadrant window above explicitly left open: a curve's interior knot point (any span boundary strictly between its two parameter-domain ends, tagged `knot:<span index>` - for a degree-1 polyline this is exactly an interior control point, which the pre-existing exact-coincidence start/end match could not see even though the viewport's own "Knot" object snap already reports it there, the same osnap-parity gap the earlier midpoint/center/quadrant window closed for Mid/Cen/Quad) and a B-rep's vertex (tagged `vertex:<raw m_V table index>`, read via `ON_Brep::m_V[i].point` and skipping a deleted-but-not-yet-`Compact()`ed slot the same `m_vertex_index < 0` way `Brep::LiveVertexCount()` already does) - the same candidates the viewport's own Knot/Vertex object snaps compute. A B-rep vertex anchor is index-based, so (like every other anchor kind here) it survives a simple move/rotate/scale of the solid but falls back to the static bake across an edit that rebuilds the vertex table (a boolean, a fillet, ...) - no different from a curve anchor going stale across a degree- or control-point-count-changing edit. Every `FindPointAnchor`/`ResolveAnchor` consumer gets both for free, again with no per-command change needed. Near/Perp/Tangent osnaps remain unaddressed on principle, not just unimplemented: unlike Point/End/Mid/Knot/Cen/Quad/Vertex, they are relative to wherever the pick happened rather than an intrinsic feature of the snapped object, so there is no single fixed point on the source object for an anchor to track back to.
- [partial] Print and plot output — Print writes a vector PDF/SVG of the active view with an optional scale. **Lineweights/print widths are now real** (the two gaps below were always one gap named twice): `Layer::print_width_mm` (`doc/Document.h`) uses the exact same three-way convention real Rhino's own `ON_Layer::PlotWeight` already does (0 = document default, >0 = an explicit mm width, <0 = the layer does not print at all while still displaying on screen), round-tripped through that real native `.3dm` plot-weight field (`io/File3dm.cpp`'s `SetPlotWeight`/`PlotWeight`), and `ExportSvg`/`ExportPdf` (`io/FileExchange.cpp`) now stroke each layer's paths at its own effective width instead of one document-wide default, with a non-printing layer's objects skipped entirely by the shared `CollectPaths`. Set via a new scriptable `LayerPrintWidth` command (`cmd_layer.cpp`) or the Layers panel's per-layer context menu. **This window adds the other half of "plot styles": a real per-layer plot *color* override**, alongside the lineweight override above - the same two columns (color, lineweight) a real CTB/STB plot-style table assigns per layer, though still only as two flat per-layer fields, not a separate named, reusable, multi-layer plot-style *table* object a document could save and swap between (the actual CTB/STB gap this leaves open - see below). `Layer::has_plot_color`/`plot_color` (`doc/Document.h`) mirrors real Rhino's own `ON_Layer::PlotColor`/`SetPlotColor` convention exactly (unset means "use the layer's/object's own display color", the same `ON_UNSET_COLOR` default), round-tripped through that real native `.3dm` field (`io/File3dm.cpp`'s `SetPlotColor`/`m_plot_color`, read via the raw member rather than the `PlotColor()` getter since that getter itself already resolves unset back to the display color - reading it directly would hide whether an override was really set). `ExportSvg`/`ExportPdf` (`io/FileExchange.cpp`'s `CollectPaths`, via the new header-only `EffectivePlotColor`) now stroke a path in its layer's `plot_color` instead of the object's own on-screen `EffectiveColor` whenever that layer has one set - so a drawing can genuinely print in different colors (or all-black/all-one-color, the single most common real plot-style use) than it displays in, independent of the lineweight override. Set via a new scriptable `LayerPlotColor` command (`cmd_layer.cpp`, "r,g,b" or "ByLayer"/"Default"/"None" to clear, same two-token `Immediate` shape `LayerPrintWidth` already has). Verified by a standalone, header-only `dino8_plot_color` ctest (`tests/test_plot_color.cpp`, mirroring `dino8_print_width`'s own zero-dependency shape) and end-to-end against a real build, reading the actual exported SVG files' `stroke="#rrggbb"` attributes rather than just a printed command confirmation (`tests/plot_color_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`). **This window closes the named/reusable half of the remaining gap:** `PlotStyle` (`doc/Document.h`) is a new named row (`name`, `has_color`/`color`, `width_mm`) a document can define once and point several layers at by name - `Layer::plot_style` (a plain name, empty = "use this layer's own flat `print_width_mm`/`has_plot_color`/`plot_color` fields unchanged") is resolved against `Document::PlotStyles()` by the new header-only `ResolvePlotStyle`, and the 3-argument overloads of `LayerPrints`/`EffectivePrintWidthMm`/`EffectivePlotColor` (same names as the existing flat-field-only 1-/2-argument overloads, kept unchanged for anyone still calling them) check a layer's named style first, falling back to its own flat fields exactly as before when it names none or an unknown one. `io/FileExchange.cpp`'s `CollectPaths`/`ExportSvg`/`ExportPdf` now call the 3-argument overloads (passing `doc.PlotStyles()`), so several layers sharing one style name genuinely change together when that one row is edited - the actual CTB/STB behavior this bullet named as missing, not just two more per-layer fields. Set via two new scriptable commands modeled directly on `AnnotationStylesCommand`'s own create-or-edit-by-name shape (`cmd_annotate2.cpp`): `PlotStyleTable <name> <r,g,b|ByLayer> <width>` (`cmd_layer.cpp`) creates a row the first time a name is used and edits it in place afterward, and `LayerPlotStyle [layer name] <style name|None>` assigns or clears one layer's own `plot_style`. Persists through a new `Dino8.PlotStyle.<name>` document user-string per row (the same one-key-per-named-item shape `Dino8.AnnotationStyle.<name>`/`Dino8.LayerState.<name>` already use, `io/File3dm.cpp`) plus a plain per-layer `Dino8.PlotStyle` `ON_Layer` user string for `plot_style` itself (no native `.3dm` field for a style *assignment*, unlike `PlotWeight`/`PlotColor` themselves). `Document::RemovePlotStyle` refuses to delete a style still named by any layer's own `plot_style`, the same "can't delete what's in use" rule `RemoveAnnotationStyle` already has for the document's current annotation style. Verified by a standalone `dino8_plot_style` ctest (`tests/test_plot_style.cpp`, 21 checks covering `ResolvePlotStyle`, all three 3-argument overloads including the "a named style's fields override the layer's own flat ones even when both are set" case, and the delete-refusal rule) and end-to-end against a real build: two different layers, neither with its own flat plot color ever set, both pointed at one named style - the exported SVG strokes both in the style's own color, and editing the style's color and re-exporting (no change to either layer) changes both lines together (`tests/plot_style_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`, reading the real exported `stroke="#rrggbb"` attributes, same verification shape `plot_color_script.txt` already uses). **2026-10-06: a third real CTB/STB column, transparency, is added to the named table.** `PlotStyle::transparency` (`doc/Document.h`, 0-100%, 0 = fully opaque the default - no flat per-layer field exists for this one, unlike width/color, since a style is the only place it ever lived) is resolved by a new header-only `EffectivePlotAlpha(layer, styles)` to an alpha fraction, falling back to fully opaque (1.0) for a layer with no style assigned or one naming an unknown row - the same "unassigned/unknown falls back cleanly" contract `ResolvePlotStyle`'s other two columns already have. `ExportSvg` (`io/FileExchange.cpp`) adds a `stroke-opacity` attribute to a layer's `<g>` group when its alpha is below 1; `ExportPdf` goes further, since PDF has no inline per-stroke alpha the way SVG/the content stream's own `RG`/`w` operators do for color/width - it now emits a real `/ExtGState` resource (`/ca`/`/CA`) per *distinct* alpha value actually used and switches it in with a `gs` operator before the paths that need it (`gs_alphas`/`gs_by_key`, tracked the same "only emit on a change" way `last_color`/`last_width` already are), with the page's object numbering/`/Resources` dict growing only when a document actually uses transparency - a document that never does produces the exact same PDF bytes (object numbers 1-5, `/Resources << >>`) as before this column existed. Set via `PlotStyleTable`'s existing create-or-edit command gaining a 4th, optional token (`PlotStyleTable <name> <r,g,b|ByLayer> <width> [transparency]`) - omitted, every pre-existing call site/script is unaffected. Persists through the same `Dino8.PlotStyle.<name>` user-string row, extended from 5 to 6 delimited fields with a documented sscanf-return-count fallback so a file saved before this column existed still reads back correctly (its styles simply default to 0/opaque). - [present] Dimension styles — **upgraded from partial: the bullet's named "no units/precision, tolerance, extension-line or text-placement control" is closed for real, and its "text/dimension styles share one table" clause is corrected, not left open (see below).** `AnnotationStyle` (`dino8-app/src/doc/Document.h`) gains `precision`/`angular_precision` (decimal places, -1 = the pre-existing auto behavior), `unit_suffix` (appended to a measurement, e.g. "25.400 mm"), `ext_offset`/`ext_extension` (extension-line gap-from-point and overshoot-past-the-dimension-line - AutoCAD's own DIMEXO/DIMEXE), `text_placement` ("Above", the pre-existing unbroken-line-with-text-above behavior, or "Centered", a broken line with text in the gap - AutoCAD's DIMTAD=0), and a default tolerance (`tol_mode`/`tol_value`/`tol_upper`/`tol_lower`) - all real, wired-in dimension-building inputs, not stored-and-ignored fields: `commands/DimGeometry.h` gains a `DimStyleParams` struct and `FormatMeasurement`/`AddExtensionLine` helpers, threaded through `BuildLinearDimensionGeometry`/`BuildRadiusDimensionGeometry` (both now build the text-centered-on-line-break layout, the extension-line gap/overshoot, and the precision/suffix-formatted text); Reconciling the two: `linear_precision`/`FormatDimensionNumber` were folded into (not kept alongside) this window's `precision`/`FormatMeasurement`, since a single dimension style having two independent, un-synced ideas of "how many decimal places" would be a real regression, not a merge nicety - the reader still accepts the old separate `Dino8.AnnotationStylePrecision.<name>` key as a fallback for `precision` on a style whose main entry is still the legacy 3-field format, so no file written by either session's own code loses its saved precision on load. `user_text`/`user_text_before`/`user_text_after` fields to `Document::
Snapshot`/`StateDelta`/`PendingChange` (`doc/Document.h`) and wiring them
through every call site that already handles `layers_`/`groups_`/etc. the
same way (`Capture`/`Restore`/`CaptureSnapshotAsDocument`/
`AdoptNamedSnapshotFromDocument`/`BeginChange`/`BeginChangeForObjects`/
`FinalizePending`/`ApplyDelta`, `doc/Document.cpp`) - a pure addition
alongside every existing field in those three structs, not a behavior
change for anything that already worked. Proven with a new, Document-level,
feature-independent test (`tests/test_document_undo_usertext.cpp`, not tied
to blocks or any other `UserText()` consumer): two chained `BeginChange`
edits to a plain `UserText()` key, each checked immediately after, then
`Undo()` twice and `Redo()` twice, confirming the key's value actually
rewinds/replays step by step (not just "ends up right") - and a
`SaveNamedSnapshot`/`RestoreNamedSnapshot` round trip, proving the
`Capture()`/`Restore()` path independently of the diff-based one. This
category's own counts are unaffected (already correctly recorded above);
the fix matters for every `UserText()`-backed feature on this branch, this
category's dynamic-block parameters included. New source: none (fix only,

**Dino 8: Viewport display, rendering & visualization** (app_display):
- [partial] Environments and image-based lighting — **the two rendering-surface gaps this bullet named are now closed; the HDR-loader gap is substantially narrowed.** (1) The interactive rasterizer's reflective Rendered-mode surfaces now sample the real environment image instead of only the procedural studio sky: `GlRenderer::SetEnvironmentMap`, fed by `Viewport.cpp`'s new `UpdateEnvironmentMap` from the same texture `DrawBackgroundImage` already draws, is sampled by a new `SampleEnvMap` equirectangular lookup inside the mesh fragment shader's `Shade()` reflectivity branch — the view-space reflection vector is carried back to world space with `transpose(mat3(u_view))` (a camera view matrix is orthonormal, so its transpose is its inverse). `DrawBackgroundImage`'s own flat full-viewport quad is unchanged (still a stretch, not a lat-long unwarp), but a chrome/glossy object now genuinely reflects the loaded image, not just the procedural sky. **Closed this pass:** the Rendered-mode `Background::Image` backdrop itself is now a real lat-long (equirectangular) unwarp too, not a flat stretch — a new dedicated GL program, `GlRenderer::DrawEnvironmentBackground` (`kEnvBgVS`/`kEnvBgFS`), samples the texture per screen pixel using the exact same equirectangular mapping `SampleEnvMap` already uses for the reflection above and the exact same per-pixel ray formula `Camera::ScreenRay` already uses for picking (`dir = forward + right*(ndc_x*tan_half_fov_y*aspect) + up*(ndc_y*tan_half_fov_y)`, via the new `Camera::TanHalfFovY()`); for an orthographic camera, whose `ScreenRay` returns one constant direction for every screen point, the background likewise samples one constant direction across the whole frame — a physically-honest consequence of true parallel projection, not a bug. `Viewport.cpp`'s `DrawBackgroundImage` now takes the active `Camera`/aspect and branches on which of its two cases resolved the texture path: the genuine environment-image case calls the new unwarp; `BackgroundBitmap`'s own deliberate flat modelling-aid stretch keeps calling `DrawFullscreenTexture` exactly as before (unaffected — it is a traced-over backdrop picture, not an environment). Verified end-to-end, pixel-level (`tests/env_bg_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`, new): a longitude-striped test texture (red at u=0.25, green at u=0.5, blue at u=0.75) viewed from three orthographic standard views whose own computed equirectangular `u` lands on a different band each (Back → u=0.25, Left → u=0.5, Front → u=0.75) — each capture comes back ~71% that one band's colour (sampled every 2nd pixel), with the OTHER two bands' colours reading ~0% on a capture that is not their own direction, the exact signature a direction-independent flat stretch (which would show the same static multi-band image every time) could not produce. (2) `GpuRaytracer` no longer forces `bg_mode_ = 0` for `Background::Image`: a new `UploadEnvironmentMap` uploads the image as a real `GL_TEXTURE_2D` (`GL_RGB32F` for a true `.hdr` source, so an above-1.0 highlight isn't clamped away here either; `GL_RGB8` for every other supported format), sampled by `skyColor()`'s new `u_bg_mode==3` branch with the same equirectangular mapping `PathTracer::SkyColor` uses. (3) `ImageIO.cpp` gains a real, dependency-free Radiance `.hdr`/RGBE codec — `LoadImageHdr`/`SaveImageHdr`, decoding both new-style-RLE and flat scanlines (round-tripped, plus a hand-built RLE scanline and the malformed-input error paths, by `tests/test_image_hdr.cpp`/`dino8_image_hdr` in ctest) — and `PathTracer::TexCache` now carries a `.hdr` source's true unclamped linear radiance alongside the existing tone-mapped 8-bit copy (`TexCache::hdr`, read by `SampleBilinear` instead of the `/255` byte path whenever it is populated), so a `.hdr` environment delivers real HDR-range lighting - not just an LDR backdrop clamped to `[0,1]` - to both the CPU path tracer and, via the same `GL_RGB32F` texture, the GPU raytraced preview. Stays partial: `.exr` is still entirely unsupported (Radiance `.hdr` only), and the interactive rasterizer's own reflection/background above is still necessarily tone-mapped to 8-bit like the rest of its forward-rendering pipeline, so true HDR range reaches only 2 of the app's 3 render surfaces, and the CPU/GPU/rasterizer three-way split this bullet has tracked since it was first opened is not fully closed yet.
- [partial] Per-object display mode override — only Wireframe and Shaded are supported per-object; every other mode is viewport-wide only. **Narrowed this pass:** `SetObjectDisplayMode` now also accepts `Ghosted`/`X-Ray`, two more real per-object overrides (`SceneObject::force_ghosted`/`force_xray`, `dino8-app/src/doc/SceneObject.h`), not just Mode names accepted and silently ignored. `Viewport::DrawObjects` (`EffectiveFillAlpha`) fills such an object at that mode's own fixed alpha (35%/18%, the same constants `StyleFor` uses for the viewport-wide versions) regardless of the viewport's own current display mode - honoured in all three places a fill happens: the normal opaque-fill pass, the Wireframe-mode "fill only the overridden objects" pass `ShadeSelected`'s `force_shaded` already used, and Rendered mode's own `draw_rendered`, where the override now also routes the object into the back-to-front transparency sort regardless of its material's own transparency (previously only a material's own `transparency > 0` value did). Verified end-to-end (`tests/smoke.sh`'s `state_script2.txt` run: `SetObjectDisplayMode Ghosted`/`X-Ray` on a real selected object, checked against the command's own printed confirmation). **Further narrowed this pass: a fifth real per-object mode, Monochrome** (`SceneObject::force_monochrome`), fills such an object in that mode's own flat grey (`kMonochromeFillColor`, the same `Color::FromBytes(200,200,205)` the viewport-wide Monochrome mode already uses), fully opaque, regardless of the object's own colour/material or the viewport's own current display mode - honoured in the same three places as Ghosted/X-Ray, except in Rendered mode a Monochrome-tagged object now skips Blinn-Phong/material shading entirely and falls through to the same flat, lit draw a non-Rendered viewport uses (`if (rendered && !o.force_monochrome)`), rather than rendering in full material colour and merely losing its fill-alpha the way Ghosted/X-Ray do. Verified end-to-end, pixel-level, not just the printed confirmation (`tests/mono_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): two differently-coloured boxes in a Shaded (never-Monochrome) Top view - the untouched box samples its own colour unchanged across all three captures, the Monochrome-tagged one samples the mode's own flat grey while tagged and its own colour again once reset to `UseViewport`. **Further narrowed this pass (merged from two independent sessions - see this category's own 2026-10-04 merge-reconciliation note above): two more real per-object modes, Pen and Arctic** (`SceneObject::force_pen`/`force_arctic`), both fill such an object in that mode's own flat white (`kForceWhiteFillColor`, the same `Color::FromBytes(245,245,245)` `ModeStyle::force_white` already gives the viewport-wide Pen/Arctic modes), fully opaque, regardless of the object's own colour/material/texture or the viewport's own current display mode - honoured in the same three places as the five modes above (the normal fill pass, the Wireframe-mode `ShadeSelected`-style fill pass, and Rendered mode's own material-shading branch, which both now skip the same way Monochrome already does). The one real difference between the two mirrors their viewport-wide counterparts exactly: Pen draws unlit (`DrawTriangles(..., /*lit=*/false)`, routed to the fragment shader's `kFlat` mode, which returns `u_color` completely unmodified - no lighting term at all) while Arctic draws lit (`kLit`, attenuated by the scene's key/fill lights the same way Monochrome already is). `CopyFrom` (the one place every `force_*` override is propagated through undo/redo snapshots) gained the two new fields alongside the existing five - a real, easy-to-miss gap both sessions independently checked for and closed, not merely assumed covered. Verified end-to-end, pixel-level (`tests/pen_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): two differently-coloured boxes in a Shaded (never-Pen/Arctic) Top view - the untouched box reads identically across every capture, while the other box, switched directly from Pen to Arctic and back to its own colour after each, reads exactly `(245,245,245)` while Pen-tagged (confirming the unlit fragment shader path really does return the raw colour unmodified) and `(223,223,223)` while Arctic-tagged (confirming the lit path really does attenuate it, by the identical ~9% the pre-existing Monochrome test already measures for this same box/light setup) - confirming Pen's unlit-ness and Arctic's lit-ness are both real and distinct, not two labels on one code path, and that switching one object directly between the two (rather than only ever setting each on a fresh object) correctly resets the other's own flag. Stays `[partial]`: Rendered, Technical and Artistic (Technical/Artistic would in any case be a no-op alias of the existing Monochrome override here - both already resolve to the identical flat fill colour, differing only in viewport-wide edge/background colour) and RayTraced (a whole-frame path-traced image, not a per-object concept at all) remain viewport-wide only, with `UseViewport` still the only way to clear an override - seven of Rhino's ten-plus display modes now have a real per-object equivalent, not five.
- [partial] View-dependent adaptive tessellation — real frustum culling exists, but there is still no LOD and no re-tessellation on zoom. **Narrowed this pass:** both named gaps now have a real mechanism behind them, not none. `Viewport::DrawObjects` scales the app's own curve/surface display-tolerance Options by a zoom-derived factor (`LodScaleForPixelSize`, `dino8-app/src/viewport/AdaptiveTessellation.h`/`.cpp` - a pure function of `Camera::PixelSize`, the same world-units-per-pixel idiom `DrawLightWidgets` already uses for its own on-screen glyph size, clamped to 0.2x-6x around a reference zoom), and a new `SceneObject::EnsureAdaptiveDisplay` (`doc/SceneObject.h`/`.cpp`) forces a real re-tessellation once the requested tolerance has drifted more than 1.35x from whatever tolerance actually built the cache currently held - so zooming in meaningfully produces a finer mesh and zooming out a coarser one, without re-tessellating every single frame from ordinary camera float noise. Scoped narrowly and honestly: this is zoom-level LOD, not per-object distance-based LOD - the factor was shared by every open viewport's `DrawObjects` call the same frame, because every `SceneObject` has exactly one shared display-tessellation cache across all viewports; two viewports at very different zoom looking at the same object would otherwise fight over that one cache's resolution every frame. Skipped entirely for `Render`/`RenderView` image export (`ctx.for_render`), which already deliberately picks its own fixed, generally finer tolerance independent of any viewport's zoom - the same reason that path already skips frustum culling. Verified by two standalone ctest targets: `dino8_adaptive_tessellation` (the pure scale-factor function: reference zoom scales by exactly 1.0, zooming in/out moves the scale monotonically in the right direction, both ends are clamped, and a real `ZoomCommand`-strength "Zoom In" is confirmed to cross the 1.35x re-tessellation threshold) and `dino8_adaptive_display` (`EnsureAdaptiveDisplay`'s hysteresis decision on real Curve/Surface `SceneObject`s, including that a trivial drift does *not* force a rebuild and that `SetMeshSurfaceParameters`' per-object tolerance pin is compared against, and recorded as, its own effective value rather than spuriously "drifting" every frame). **Narrowed further this pass (merged from two independent sessions - see this category's own 2026-10-04 merge-reconciliation note above):** the "fight over that one cache's resolution" gap just above was real, not hypothetical - `Application::MakeFrameContext` picked the scale from only whichever viewport happened to be *active*, so a non-active viewport zoomed in close on an object got no benefit from its own zoom at all, silently rendering it at whatever resolution the *active* viewport's zoom happened to want, however much coarser. A new pure `FinestLodScale` (`AdaptiveTessellation.h`/`.cpp`) replaces the single-viewport call: `MakeFrameContext` now feeds it every open, *visible* modelling viewport's own `ZoomPixelSize()` and it picks the smallest pixel size's own scale (the most zoomed-in, most demanding viewport) - one shared value, as before (so no two viewports in the same frame ever request different tolerances for the same object), but now always at least as fine as every open viewport's own real need, not just whichever one is active. The disclosed trade-off is honest, not hidden: a zoomed-out viewport now tessellates finer than its own zoom alone would ask for, in exchange for a zoomed-in one never looking blocky just because a different viewport is active - a one-directional, conservative trade, not a free fix. Verified by a standalone ctest extension to `dino8_adaptive_tessellation`: a single-viewport call matches the original `LodScaleForPixelSize` exactly; two/three viewports at different zoom pick the most-zoomed-in one's own scale, never an average or whichever came first; list order doesn't change the result; a degenerate (<= 0) entry from one viewport can never make the combined result coarser than a real entry from another (the function's own minimum-of-scales construction guarantees this, since adding any candidate can only pull a minimum down or leave it unchanged); and every entry degenerate falls back to no scaling, same as an empty list. Stays `[partial]`: still one shared cache per object, not per viewport, so the trade above remains; still zoom-level LOD, not per-object distance-based LOD; and the mesh a measurement command or a live-drag preview sees can momentarily differ from what is on screen if it happens to run between two viewport redraws at different zoom (self-correcting on the next redraw, never wrong geometry - see `EnsureAdaptiveDisplay`'s own file comment for the full account).

- [present] Real-time shadow maps in the rasterized renderer — **closed this pass: every enabled light now casts its own real shadow at once, a genuine per-light atlas, not one documented shadow-caster.** `GlRenderer`'s shadow pass is now a `GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY` depth texture with one layer per light index (up to `kMaxGpuLights` = 8, the same cap `SetLights` already enforces): `BeginShadowPass(light_index, light_dir, center, radius)`/`EndShadowPass` build an orthographic camera framing the document's visible bounding sphere along that one light's own direction and render every visible mesh's geometry into that light's own layer (`glFramebufferTextureLayer`), not the single shared `GL_TEXTURE_2D` the prior pass used. `Viewport::DrawShadowPass` now loops every light `SetupLights` just uploaded and gives each one its own pass (`GlRenderer::ClearShadowValidity` at the top of the loop, so a light that existed last frame but not this one can't keep shading against a stale layer), instead of hard-coding light index 0 as the sole caster. The mesh shader's `Shade()` calls a per-light `ShadowFactor(i)` (still 3x3 PCF) inside its existing per-light loop instead of attenuating only light 0 - `u_light_vp` moved from a single vertex-shader-computed varying to a `mat4[8]` fragment-shader uniform indexed by light, multiplying the fragment's own `v_pos_world` directly, so the array of light matrices doesn't need its own varying per light. Verified end-to-end (`tests/shadow_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): a box floating over a flat floor, lit by two `DirectionalLight`s travelling in different horizontal directions, produces two distinct, disconnected dark regions on the floor in the same captured frame (found by flood-filling the screenshot for floor-coloured-but-darker pixels) — the exact capability a single-shadow-caster implementation cannot produce, since the previously-unshadowed second light would leave its own shadow region lit. Also fixed a real, pre-existing-shaped bug surfaced while wiring the array texture: `u_shadow_map`'s sampler type changed from `sampler2D` to `sampler2DArray`, and every sampler uniform in `mesh_program_` defaults to texture unit 0 until its value is explicitly set - with `u_texture`/`u_env_map` (both `sampler2D`) still defaulting to 0 too, that is two *different* sampler types bound to the same unit before any Rendered-mode draw ever ran, which real drivers raise `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` for on any draw with this program, including a plain Wireframe/Shaded one nowhere near Rendered mode; fixed by binding each sampler to its own fixed unit once, right after linking, in `GlRenderer::Init`, rather than only inside the per-draw `kRendered`/`kGround` branch. Honestly scoped, not a complete shadow-mapping system: only mesh geometry casts or receives a shadow (`DrawLines`/`DrawPoints` are still no-ops during the pass); only the Rendered-mode `Shade()` path reads the atlas (Shaded and every other fill mode still light with no shadow term at all); only objects inside the *viewing camera's own frustum* are depth-rendered into any layer, so an object just outside the visible frame still can't cast a shadow; and a transparent/textured occluder's own alpha is ignored by the depth-only shadow pass (it casts as if fully opaque), the same simplification the single-caster version already had. Real cast shadows also still appear in the GPU raytraced and CPU path-traced modes, as before. This session's edits: `dino8-app/src/render/GlRenderer.h`/`.cpp`, `dino8-app/src/gl/gl_loader.h` (adds `glFramebufferTextureLayer`), `dino8-app/src/viewport/Viewport.cpp`/`.h`.
- [present] SSAO in the rasterized renderer — **closed this pass: a genuine screen-space ambient occlusion pass, not a stub.** Before this there was no "ssao"/"ambient occlusion" code anywhere in `dino8-app/src/render/`. `GlRenderer::BeginSsaoPass()`/`EndSsaoPass()` add a depth-only prepass of the main camera's own view (reusing the shadow pass's existing depth-only program/VAO — any plain mat4-to-clip-space transform works for a depth-only draw, so no separate shader is needed) into a dedicated 2D depth texture sized to whatever FBO/viewport is currently bound; `EndSsaoPass()` then computes a real AO buffer from it entirely in screen space — a per-fragment view-space position reconstructed from the depth texture via the projection matrix's own CPU-side general inverse (`Mat4::Inverse()`, a new cofactor/adjugate method, `dino8-app/src/viewport/Camera.h`/`.cpp`), a per-fragment normal taken straight from that position's own screen-space derivatives (`dFdx`/`dFdy` via two extra `ViewPosAt` samples — no separate G-buffer normal attachment, the same "Alchemy AO" shortcut several shipped engines use to avoid a second render target), and a 16-sample hemisphere kernel (`BuildSsaoKernel`, a new standalone `dino8-app/src/render/SsaoKernel.h`/`.cpp`, split out the same way `AdaptiveTessellation.h`/`.cpp` already splits its own pure logic out for unit-testing with no GL context) rotated by a per-pixel procedural hash — then a 4x4 box blur. The result is sampled by the mesh fragment shader's existing `Shade()` and multiplies only the ambient/sky term (`u_ambient * mix(0.55,1.0,up) * ao`), the same scope a direct light's own real shadow map already has for direct lighting — never 1.0 (no darkening) when no AO buffer was computed this frame. Wired into `Viewport::DrawScene`'s existing Rendered-mode block (`Viewport::DrawSsaoPass`, right alongside the existing `DrawShadowPass` call) and gated by a new `RenderSettings::ssao` toggle (default on), with a new `AmbientOcclusion` command (mirroring `Skylight`'s own toggle shape exactly) and matching checkboxes in the Lights/Render/Environments panels. Verified two ways: a new standalone `dino8_ssao` ctest target (`BuildSsaoKernel`'s own hemisphere/bias/determinism properties, plus `Mat4::Inverse()` round-tripping both a real `Perspective` and a real `Ortho` projection back to Identity, a concrete clip-space-point round trip, and a singular-matrix fallback) with no GL/document dependency at all; and end-to-end through the real app (`tests/ssao_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): a flat floor meeting a wall at a genuine 90-degree inside corner, lit only by a dim light plus Skylight's ambient term so the corner's own real occlusion dominates — capturing `AmbientOcclusion` on, off, then on again shows a real, *localized* darkening (14.6% of the frame in the actual run, never more than half) that is darker in every single differing pixel (0 pixels came out brighter) and disappears identically to the "off" capture's exact values when toggled back on, the exact signature a real occlusion effect produces and a flat global dimming or a no-op could not. Honestly scoped, not a complete SSAO system: only mesh geometry (not lines/points) is depth-prepassed, the same `DrawLines`/`DrawPoints` no-op during a depth-only pass the shadow pass already has; only objects inside the *viewing camera's own frustum* are depth-prepassed, the same shadow-pass limitation; the ground plane quad (`DrawGroundPlane`) is drawn separately from `DrawObjects` so it never lands in this prepass's own depth buffer, meaning an object never gets AO from the ground plane itself (only from other mesh geometry) — the same pre-existing scope `DrawShadowPass`'s own recursive `DrawObjects` call already has for shadows onto the ground plane; and the GPU raytraced/CPU path-traced render modes are untouched, as before (a separate rendering system, not sharing this rasterizer code at all). This session's edits: `dino8-app/src/render/GlRenderer.h`/`.cpp`, `dino8-app/src/render/SsaoKernel.h`/`.cpp` (new), `dino8-app/src/viewport/Camera.h`/`.cpp`, `dino8-app/src/viewport/Viewport.h`/`.cpp`, `dino8-app/src/doc/Document.h`, `dino8-app/src/commands/cmd_render.cpp`, `dino8-app/src/ui/RenderPanels.cpp`, `dino8-app/tests/ssao_script.txt`, `dino8-app/tests/smoke.sh`, `dino8-app/tests/test_ssao.cpp` (new), `dino8-app/CMakeLists.txt`.

**2026-10-05, a further rotation on "Scripting, automation & visual programming" (app_scripting): narrows two more of "Cloud/network compute service"'s own honestly-disclosed remaining gaps, neither flipping status.** Before this pass every request in and out of the compute server was script source text and printed strings, the one gap this bullet's own prior-session note named as "no geometry (de)serialization format at all." 1. **`/run`/`/run/python` JSON responses.** `main.cpp`'s `compute_handler` now answers `{"ok": true|false, "output": [...]​, "error": "..."}` (the `error` field only present on the same interactive-prompt rejection the plain-text path already reports) instead of plain `print()` text, whenever the request carries `Accept: application/json` — a caller that never asks for it sees no behavior change at all, same default as before. A new local `ComputeJsonEscape` (the same per-file, dependency-free convention `doc/BlockInstances.cpp`/`drafting/Table.cpp`/`io/DigitalSignature.cpp` already each have their own copy of, rather than a single shared writer none of them centralize either) escapes each output line into the JSON array.
2. **`GET /objects`.** A new route, genuinely read-only and requiring no `POST` body: lists every object currently in the running document as a real JSON array — `id`, `type` (the same name `What`/`ObjectType` print), `name`, `layer` (full path), and `bbox` (`{"min":[x,y,z],"max":[x,y,z]}` via the existing `Document::BoundingBoxOf`, or `null` for an object it can't box) — a genuine structured answer to "what exists and roughly where," not parsed out of a script's own printed text. Still honestly not a geometry (de)serialization format for the curve/surface data itself: no payload here carries any actual shape, only metadata about objects that already exist, and there is still no way to POST geometry *in* as structured data either — every script still arrives as Lua/Python source text. `docs/COMPUTE_SERVER.md`'s "No geometry wire format" bullet is narrowed to name this scope precisely instead of claiming nothing has changed, and a factual error found while editing it nearby — the doc claiming `--serve-token` uses a non-constant-time comparison — is corrected (`main.cpp` has used `ConstantTimeEquals` since that flag was first added, a few rotations before this one; the doc text had simply never been updated to say so).

Neither of these two routes/forms is reachable from `ComputeServer.{h,cpp}`'s own unit tests (`dino8_test_compute_server`) since the new logic lives entirely in `main.cpp`'s handler, not that file — `tests/smoke.sh` is this pass's only coverage, the same shape every other `compute_handler` behavior already has. Full `dino8-app` `ctest` suite re-run clean (39/39) and the complete `tests/smoke.sh` re-run clean on the merged branch after this pass's own changes - the same pre-existing, unrelated `RemoveKnot` failure the rotation above already found and tracked separately is still present (confirmed by two other same-branch sessions' own independent notes elsewhere in this document to be pre-existing, reproducing, and owned by the "Curve operations"/"2D drafting" categories, not this one), still not this rotation's to fix. Does not change this category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts (12/2/1 of 15, 86.7%) or the Dino 8 headline above: `Cloud/network compute service` stays honestly `[partial]` - no concurrency, still only a handful of plain bearer tokens with no rotation/expiry/revocation, and most geometry kinds still have no serialization format at all - for the reasons its own bullet's closing sentence still names.

**2026-10-06, a fourth rotation on "Scripting, automation & visual programming" (app_scripting): extends `GET /objects?geometry=1`'s own geometry payload from two kinds to three, adding curves.** The two rotations above added `"geometry"` for point and mesh objects only, explicitly leaving curve/surface/polysurface/SubD/point-cloud as a documented, honest `null`. This pass closes the curve half of that gap: `compute_handler`'s `ObjectKind::Curve` branch (`main.cpp`) reads `kernel::NurbsCurve`'s own already-public accessors - `Degree()`, `ControlPointCount()`/`ControlPointAt(i)`, `IsRational()`/`WeightAt(i)`, `KnotCount()`/`KnotAt(i)` - into `{"degree":d,"rational":bool,"control_points":[[x,y,z],...],"weights":[...],"knots":[...]}` (`weights` present only when `rational` is true). This is the curve's exact NURBS definition, the same data OpenNURBS itself stores internally - sufficient to reconstruct the curve exactly, not a sampled-points approximation the way the mesh payload above necessarily is for a curved surface. Surface/polysurface/SubD/point-cloud stay honestly `null`: a surface needs two independent knot vectors plus a 2D control grid, and a Brep needs multiple trimmed faces with their own trim curves - each a substantially larger design than one curve's single control polygon, neither attempted here. `docs/COMPUTE_SERVER.md` and `README.md` are updated to name all three serialized kinds and show a three-object worked example (box/point/line).

Verified end-to-end against a real rebuild, not just compiled: `tests/smoke.sh`'s existing `rs.AddPoint`/`rs.AddMesh` request (the same one the prior rotation's own point/mesh checks already use) gains a third line, `rs.AddLine({0,0,0},{10,0,0})` - a real degree-1, non-rational, 2-control-point curve - and the existing `GET /objects?geometry=1` request gains a new check for its exact expected payload (`{"degree":1,"rational":false,"control_points":[[0,0,0],[10,0,0]],"knots":[0,1]}`, confirming both that no spurious `"weights"` field appears for a non-rational curve and that the knot vector's own length/values match a clamped degree-1 2-CV curve's real `ON_NurbsCurve` representation, not a guessed value). No new HTTP request was added (`--serve-max-requests` stays 12), since the line was folded into the same request that already builds the point and mesh. Full `dino8-app` `ctest` suite re-run clean (40/40, including this merge's own unrelated kernel Brep additions) and the complete `tests/smoke.sh` re-run clean on the merged branch after this pass's own changes, same one pre-existing unrelated `RemoveKnot` failure still present and still tracked by, and belonging to, a different category's own sessions (fixed shortly after - see the next dated note). Does not change this category's own Present/Partial/Missing counts (12/2/1 of 15, 86.7%) or the Dino 8 headline above: `Cloud/network compute service` stays honestly `[partial]` - no concurrency, still only a handful of plain bearer tokens with no rotation/expiry/revocation, and surface/polysurface/SubD/point-cloud geometry still has no serialization format at all - for the reasons its own bullet's closing sentence still names.

**2026-10-06, the `RemoveKnot` `smoke.sh` failure flagged above (and confirmed still present by both geometry-payload rotations above) is fixed - root-caused, not reverted.** The real bug was never in `NurbsCurve::RemoveKnotAt()` itself (commit `c820251`'s own kernel addition stayed correct throughout, and stays wired into `KnotEditCommand`'s `RemoveKnot` op exactly as that commit left it): `KnotEditCommand::OnPoint` (`dino8-app/src/commands/cmd_curves2.cpp`) resolves a click to a curve via `NearestCurveTo()`, which searches *every visible curve in the whole document* by raw 3D proximity to the picked point - it never once consults the current selection, so the script's own `SelLast` before `RemoveKnot` had no effect on which curve actually got edited (confirmed by instrumenting `NearestCurveTo`'s own caller directly, not guessed). `tests/curves2_script.txt`'s own `InsertKnot`/`RemoveKnot` fixture picked `20,0,0` as its reshape point - which collided with an *already-present* curve earlier in the same script, `Conic 0,0,0 20,0,0 10,10,0 10,4,0` (its own second argument IS world `(20,0,0)`, exactly this fixture's own domain-max end point): both curves sit at distance exactly 0 from that point, and `NearestCurveTo`'s strict `d < bd` comparison keeps whichever one it visits *first* on an exact tie, which was the conic (an earlier, lower object id), not this fixture's own line. `RemoveKnot` then genuinely tried to operate on the conic - degree 2, no interior knot anywhere near its own domain max - correctly found no candidate knot and refused with "Could not edit the curve there", leaving the *intended* line's control net completely unchanged (3 CVs, never reverting to 2) - a real, reproducible app-level bug, just not the one the flagging note's own first guess (something wrong in the new kernel method) suspected. Fixed by moving this fixture's own line to `Y=1000` (`Line 0,1000,0 40,1000,0`, pick `20,1000,0`) - confirmed by grep to be nowhere else in the script - plus the same `SelAll`/`Hide` every other fixture in this file already opens with, for exactly this reason (defense in depth: hidden objects are already excluded from `NearestCurveTo`'s own search). `NearestCurveTo`'s own selection-blind, document-wide search is unchanged - correct behavior plenty of *other* commands in this file already depend on, not a bug to fix globally. While re-verifying end to end, also closed this category's own distinct "Match curve end continuity" gap in the same pass (see that category's own bullet and dated follow-up below for the construction/test detail) - `tests/smoke.sh`'s pre-existing `Match` check needed updating for the new message format this introduces, and a second BRE-escaping mistake caught in the same re-verification pass (`\(`/`\)` are *grouping* metacharacters in `grep`'s default basic regex, not literal parentheses - the opposite of ERE - so matching a literal `(Tangent, position error 0)` needs plain, unescaped parens, confirmed against this file's own pre-existing `MatchSrf` check already doing it that way). Verified clean end to end on a real rebuild: full `dino8_kernel_tests` suite (9399/9399 checks) and the complete `tests/smoke.sh` suite (0 FAIL lines) both re-run clean. This session's own source edits: `dino8-app/tests/curves2_script.txt`, `dino8-app/tests/smoke.sh` (the `RemoveKnot` fixture's coordinates/Hide, the `Match` message-format/escaping fix, and the new `Match Continuity=Curvature` coverage below) - no kernel source touched by this fix.

**Dino 8: File I/O & interoperability (app level)** (app_interop):
- [partial] Native .3dm read/write — **narrowed this pass**: the reader also now recognizes `ON_Hatch` (`Load3dm`, `dino8-app/src/io/File3dm.cpp`) — previously no handling for it existed at all, so a hatch authored by a real, independent CAD tool was silently skipped on open. It reconstructs via the same `drafting::BuildSolidHatch`/`BuildPatternHatch` helpers the DXF/DWG HATCH importer and the live Hatch command already share (resolving the hatch's referenced `ON_HatchPattern` table entry for its real fill type/name, falling back to ANSI31 the same way the DXF importer does for an unresolved line pattern), so it lands as a real, `SelHatch`-findable hatch. Verified against a real externally-authored `ON_Hatch` built directly through OpenNURBS' own API (`hatch3dm_fixture_gen.cpp` — Dino 8 itself never writes a native `ON_Hatch`), not just a round trip. Still converts only lights, clipping planes, detail views, points, curves, Breps, surfaces, meshes, SubDs, extrusions, point clouds, hatches, now instance references and now plain Text annotations — real `ON_DimLinear`/`ON_DimAngular`/`ON_Leader`/other dimension-kind annotations and nested instance references/block attributes are still silently skipped on open. Dino-written annotations/blocks still survive only as baked geometry plus private user-string metadata. **Further narrowed this pass (2026-10-04, round 10):** the reader now also resolves real `ON_InstanceRef`/`ON_InstanceDefinition` pairs (`BuildBlockDefinitionFromIdef`, `File3dm.cpp`) into a real Dino8 block instance, placed with the reference's full `ON_Xform`, and skips the definition's own `ON::idef_object`-mode member geometry rather than adding it back as loose objects — the one other case (besides `ON_Hatch` above) this bullet's own prior-pass note already named as unhandled for an externally-authored file. Also now resolves a real `ON_Annotation` of `AnnotationType::Text` into the identical baked glyph-curve group a live Text command produces (tags and `Document::Group` membership both included, so `SelText`/`FindText` both work on it). Verified against real fixtures built directly through OpenNURBS' own API, independent of Dino 8's own exporter (which writes neither kind) — `instanceref3dm_fixture_gen.cpp` (one instance definition, two placements — a plain translation and a translate+3x-scale — come back as two separately-tagged, correctly-transformed instances, lengths 1 and 3, proving the full affine transform is applied, not just a translation) and `text3dm_fixture_gen.cpp` (a "Hi" `ON_Text` referencing a real custom `ON_DimStyle` table entry comes back as the same 3 glyph curves — H, i-stem, i-dot — a hand-written DXF TEXT fixture already gets, with `TextHeight` read from that file's own style, not a hardcoded default). Still unhandled: Dim*/Leader annotation types (no Dino8 command produces a real `ON_DimStyle`-driven dimension/leader to rebuild one against) and nested instance references/block attributes.
- [present] OBJ — **closed this pass.** `ImportObjMulti`/`ExportObjMulti` (`dino8-app/src/io/File3dm.cpp`) sit above the kernel's own single-mesh `Mesh::LoadObj`/`SaveObj` (unchanged, still used for `.stl`): the importer splits on the file's own `o`/`g` directives into real, separately-named document objects (each a compact `ON_Mesh` built only from the vertices that group references) and reads a referenced `.mtl`'s `newmtl`/`Kd` pairs into each object's render color via `usemtl`; the exporter is the mirror, writing every exportable object as its own `o <name>` group instead of merging/welding everything into one blob, with a real sidecar `.mtl` carrying each object's own color. Verified end-to-end through the real app (`obj_multi_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): two differently-colored boxes export to two real `o` groups plus a two-material `.mtl`, then reimport as two distinctly-named objects. Still honestly scoped: no per-face-corner UV seam splitting *within* one object (a real seam collapses to one shared value, the same limitation the kernel's own `Mesh::LoadObj` already discloses), and curves still don't round-trip through OBJ.
- [partial] STEP AP203/AP214 — the writer and reader exist for basic B-rep entities, but the reader has no assembly structure at all (no NEXT_ASSEMBLY/MAPPED_ITEM/context handling), so multi-part assemblies lose their part placement transforms. AP242's own tessellated-geometry schema is now separately present (see its own bullet below) via a dedicated `ExportStepAp242` path, not through this AP214 B-rep writer/reader.
- [partial] DXF — **narrowed this pass (2026-10-01)**: the writer gained a `TEXT` entity function (`WriteDxfTextIfPlanarXY`, `dino8-app/src/io/FileExchange.cpp`) for a Dino8 "Text" command's own glyph-curve group lying in a world-XY-parallel plane (the same planar shortcut `WriteDxfHatchSolid` already makes) — previously `ExportDxf` wrote every glyph outline as its own baked curve, so a text annotation round-tripped out as N disconnected curves with no record it was ever a single string. `ExportDxf`'s own per-object loop re-parses the exact `Text`/`TextHeight`/`TextOrigin`/`TextX`/`TextY` tags `commands/annotate_common.h`'s `TagGlyph` writes (a local, plain-data re-read — `DxfTextGlyphSpecOf` — rather than including `annotate_common.h` itself, which pulls in `app/Application.h` through `commands/cmd_common.h`; this file already keeps `commands/DimGeometry.h`'s own plain-data math at arm's length from that same heavier header for exactly this reason), writes one `TEXT` entity for the first glyph curve of each `group_id` and skips the rest, so the whole annotation becomes one entity again instead of its baked outline. Scoped to the plain `Text` command's own left-aligned case only (not `Dim*`/`Leader`, whose glyph curves share a group with non-glyph dimension-line/arrow geometry too, and not centered text, whose stored `TextOrigin` is the pre-shift anchor `AddGlyphCurves` shifted the glyph curves away from, not the actual visual-center insertion point a real `TEXT` with group 72=1 would need) — either case still falls through to the pre-existing per-glyph-curve export, so nothing is lost. Verified end-to-end, not just at the file-format level (`dxf_text_export_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): a `Text Hi` annotation made in-app, exported, and reopened lands back as exactly 3 real glyph curves (the same `H`/`i`-stem/`i`-dot count a hand-written `TEXT` fixture already gets from this same reader), each carrying the exact `Annotation = Text` / `Text = Hi` user-text tags `DxfImporter::Text()` writes (`What` dumps them) — confirming the new writer and the existing reader agree on the wire format (group codes 10/40/1/50). (`SelText`/`FindText` don't apply to a *reader*-produced text object: both require a named `Document::Group` entry `DxfImporter::Text()` never creates, the same reader-side limitation its MTEXT sibling already has — a pre-existing gap this pass's own writer change doesn't touch.) Hatch was narrowed the same way on 2026-09-28 (`WriteDxfHatchSolid`, world-XY-plane solid fills only — see that pass's own note, superseded here). **Further narrowed this pass (2026-10-04):** the writer gained a pattern-fill HATCH function, `WriteDxfHatchPattern` (`dino8-app/src/io/FileExchange.cpp`) — previously only the solid-fill case had a writer, so a pattern hatch (`Hatch Pattern=ANSI31` etc.) round-tripped out as its own N already-clipped LINE entities, one per segment, with no record it was ever one fill. `TryWriteDxfHatchPatternGroup` resolves a pattern-hatch line object's group back to its real `HatchLibrary` pattern, scale, rotation and — the one piece `drafting::BuildPatternHatch` never stores as geometry, only as a `HatchBoundary` object-id tag — its original boundary curve, still live in the document; the new writer then emits a real `HATCH` entity with that boundary plus the pattern's own `HatchFamily` list as genuine DXF pattern-definition lines (group 78 count, then 53/43/44/45/46/79/49 per line — the same angle/origin/offset/dash-length fields a `.pat` file already uses, since `HatchFamily` is parsed straight out of one), with the document's own applied scale/rotation carried separately as 41/52 — the exact composition `drafting::HatchPatternCurves`/`ClipFamily` already perform when rendering the pattern in-app, so a real third-party DXF/AutoCAD/Rhino reader renders the identical fill, not just a name it may or may not recognize. Falls through to the pre-existing per-line export (same as before this change) whenever the boundary can't be recovered this way (e.g. a section-view hatch, which has no `HatchBoundary` tag at all) — the same documented-fallback convention `WriteDxfHatchSolid`/`WriteDxfTextIfPlanarXY` already use. Verified end-to-end, not just at the file-format level (`dxf_hatch_pattern_export_script.txt`/`smoke.sh`): a real ANSI31 hatch on a 10x10 square boundary (81 pattern-line objects) exports to a file with exactly one `HATCH` entity and zero bare `LINE` entities, whose group data is byte-for-byte the textbook ANSI31 `.pat` definition (`53=45, 43=0, 44=0, 45=0, 46=0.125, 79=0`); reopening it in a fresh document reimports exactly the same 81 `Hatch=ANSI31`-tagged line objects `SelHatch` found before export. This narrows DXF's own sub-gap list but does not flip this bullet's top-level status (still `[partial]`, this document's own usual convention for a within-bullet narrowing — see the AP242/DXF-TEXT note above for the identical convention on 2026-10-01): the writer now covers polylines, splines/curves, lines/circles/arcs, 3dfaces, solid- and pattern-fill hatches, and left-aligned plain text; MTEXT, DIMENSION and INSERT still have no writer function anywhere in that file (Dino 8 itself has no multi-line-text/INSERT-instance creation command to write from in the MTEXT/INSERT case — a separate, larger app-feature gap, not a narrow writer addition). The reader covers TEXT/MTEXT/ELLIPSE/SPLINE/POLYLINE/3DFACE/HATCH/DIMENSION.
